This is an extremely solid action/fighting game that will be a big hit with Naruto heads, and the fighting is strong enough that it’ll probably have a lot of appeal for non-fans.
The single-player story mode is an adaptation of the Fourth Shinobi War storyline from late in the series. Unfortunately, this is where the story went downhill (in my opinion, at least), and it’s so late in the series that newcomers will have no idea of what’s going on. You need to watch the show or play the other Ninja Storm games to catch up. However, while this may not be the most interesting part of the series and it’s not a great entry point for people who aren’t already in the know, it’s a very well-made adaptation. Everything about the presentation and storytelling is fantastic, from the clean, sharp take on the show’s iconic character designs to the great music to the crisp colors to the exciting action scene direction. I’d go so far as to say that, in some ways, this game is a better adaptation of the manga than the anime. The only odd thing is that so many scenes suddenly break out into a fight, while the same scenes from the manga ended in a conversation or happened without a confrontation.
But that makes sense, I guess: the action is what you’re here for. I’m a bit surprised to say that this is one of the best 3D fighting systems I’ve ever seen. Each battle is a 1 on 1, fighting game-style match in a 3D arena where you can run around and set up traps, decide on your strategy, etc. I thought that the big arenas would be cumbersome and a pain to move around it, but they worked extremely well to help manage the ebb and flow of each battle. The controls are super smooth and work like a dream. I would love to see CyberConnect 2 use this engine/fighting system in the service of another anime series like One Piece or My Hero Academia. It's not just that the fighting system is great - when you're done with the single player campaign and switch over to fighting single battles, you've got a huge cast of characters to choose from. Pretty much every major Naruto character here, as well as multiple versions of many of them (young, old, sage form, etc.), and they've all been really lovingly recreated from the anime.
I simply didn’t expect the fighting system to be this good and fun. When fighting game aficionados talk about the best 3D fighting games out there, when does anyone ever mention the Ultimate Ninja Storm series? People are sleeping on this, seriously. I really think that non-fans will find a lot to enjoy with this game. If you like 3D fighting games, Ultimate Ninja Storm 3 has a unique take on the genre that just feels like a breath of fresh air. Yes, you won’t really have any attachment to the characters, but I have a feeling that playing the game will inspire you to go seek out the original source material. Now, I know that it's a lot to ask - I'm asking you to put down some cash and spend some time on something from a franchise that you aren't into. I can already see you shaking your head "no"...but seriously, give this a chance. Get it on sale, for sure (I think I got it on sale for 7 or 8 dollars), but give it a chance. If you're already a Naruto fan, this is a much easier sell. You'll enjoy the heck out of it, trust me.
There are definitely a few flaws here, though. I think that the RPG elements of the game are extremely light and kind of pointless. There’s a bit of exploration and you get to run around a few set pieces, but that’s just to break up the formula of *extremely long series of cut-scenes followed up by a fight*. I didn't really feel compelled to do all the side quests or go talk to everyone in the town...these RPG aspects just felt half-baked and underdeveloped. It's like the studio wanted to make a Naruto RPG, but then they realized that they just wanted to leave it as a fighting game and didn't know how to take out the RPG stuff. It's not the end of the world, but yeah, this part of the game is kind of flat for me. There were also a few scenes where you run through a series of rooms and fight generic enemies: these moments were also pretty meh. The game encourages you to press a button at the right moment during these battles, so they can feel more like a quick-time event than a true expression of hack and slash action. I see what CyberConnect2 was going for here, but it's not a fully-realized idea.

Classic fairy tales meet gothic style cartoon visuals in this adventure/fragmented object game. The stories may drag on a bit too long, and the puzzles are more of a bump in the road rather than an obstacle, but it is still really fun.
In Witch’s Pranks: Frog’s Fortune, three classic Grimm tales – Briar Rose, Snow White and Rapunzel – meet in a setting that looks like something from a Tim Burton animated show. Everything is crooked, the scenery and story provide lots of (mostly kid-friendly) dark humour, and even the whole premise is completely nonsensical: you play as a nondescript hero who helps three cursed frog princes to turn back to human by finding their princesses.
Despite looking like a hidden object game, it is actually a lightweight point ‘n’ click adventure with a few simple fragmented object scenes. You need to run around the levels a lot, and some of the items are hidden a little more than they should, but none of the puzzles pose any real challenge, despite their large variety. The game just lets you enjoy the art style and funny story, and this is what I advise for anyone who gets this little gem.

You wake up on a dock. You board a strange boat. You have to meet people to retrieve their tickets to satisfy the captain. But everything is strange: between the passengers with masks, items floating in the air and the shadows, you're asking yourself if you're in the realm of Death or it's just a dream...
Port of Call is a small adventure game, in a cartoonish style, where you're trying to find who you are and why you need to meet these passengers. Listening to their stories is also interesting because they hold the key to your identity.
The soundtrack is good, like the graphics that are so reassuring and freakening at the same time: while it's not a dark game, when you see floating stuffs, a huge toy sheet and shadows, you're asking yourself what's happening. You understand quickly that you're maybe dead but then, why are you collecting tickets? Shouldn't you be a simple passenger?
Anyway, there are no puzzles there: apart speaking, finding a teddy bear and mixing drinks, you're just confronted to a poor gameplay. Yet, the dialogues here are important if you want to understand the story and find answers. The quest for the pencils and the paintings is also a nice bonus, though that for the paintings, it's very easy.
The main problem of the game is the fact that you have an hard time to find a menu, you have to press Escape to make it appear and to quit properly the game. The screen title lacks options.

While the fix for comfort is to move the mouse and to keep pressing on W, as it's not natural  to press the W instead of the Z, once you're releasing the key, you have some seconds to remind yourself, that no, the key you're so used to press isn't the same.

Every once in a while it's nice to switch to a game without time limits, stressfull shooting sequences or racing around in a car and just relax with a point and click game that's not Myst-like difficult.
Enigmatis is this type of game. It's colourfull, the graphics are decent (even the cutscenes) and the pace is whatever you want it to be.
You can see that the developers made a fair effort to make your journey through this game as pleasent as possible. Letting you skip cutscenes, decide wether you want to go after collectables or not, fast travel to areas you have been before, letting you skip puzzles if they take you too much time/effort and having a hint system that works well.
Not that the puzzles are particularly hard. They're actually quite easy. Yet, not so easy to where you don't need to think at all to solve them.
It all takes place in a bright mystical forest where you as a detective stumble upon some events that clearly need investigating. Without spoiling too much; you come across a campervan that looks like it's been in some sort of crash. When you go inside, you find a little girl hiding. As she tells you what evil has happened to her, you soon feel compelled to help out.
The characters aren't really memorable and the story isn't great, but the game does a great job in making you want to discover the magical forest and the puzzles that are within.
If you are looking to spend some time clicking away without having to think or strategise very much, this is a great game.
Buy if:
- On sale. I got it for under 5 euro's, which I think is good value
- You want to play a relatively easy point and click puzzle game
- You like bright colours and butterflies (when you play the game, you'll know what I'm talking about)
Don't buy if:
- You're expecting Myst-like difficulty
- You think it's scary/horror (it's not, even though they advertise it that way)
Positives:
- Nice graphics, bright colours, clearly has some effort put into it
- Well designed, fast travel, good hints system, can skip puzzles and cutscenes
- Easy, but not a total cakewalk
Negatives:
- Voice acting not always great, especially the main character feels like she's just reading out loud sometimes
- Story feels flat
- You spend a lot of time looking for parts of things to make them open and give you other parts for other things. --> Gets a little repetative after a while

TLDR; A very cute game with beautiful art. It relies more on a find object, use object with puzzles thrown in here and there as gameplay rather than hidden object scenes. A bit simple at times, its very kid friendly and cute and fun entertainment given a little short (3hours).
Full Review:
Gameplay 9/10
Most of the game's mechanics is finding an item and using it to advance in progress. It's used heavily and can be simple at times in that you'll often find an obstacle and find the key to it (sometimes literally a key) within a scene or two unlike other games that make you look for items and come back. So at least there's not a lot of back tracking and forgetting what you needed where. There's a good amount of puzzles and some basic hidden object scenes where the scenes are find these pictured objects instead of a list of words and are usually very simple and easy to find the objects quickly.
Plot 7/10
I'd hate to give this a low rating but it would be unfair to give it much higher considering it's a very simplistic plot. Evil witch wants a husband so she magics princes to her castle and turns them into a frog and only if they kiss their bride will they turn back into human form. So you spend the game helping the frog princes and go through fairy tale stories (three total if you include the bonus chapter)
Overall 9/10
While nothing ground breaking, it's a very cute game with very well made graphics. There a great animations and high detail in the area maps. One thing that bothered me and is very small is that it takes a small second or two for an object once revealed to be clickable. In other words, say you open a pouch of items, you'll have to wait like maybe one-two seconds before it becomes clickable to pick up the items in it. A minor thing but still worth mentioning. This is a good family friendly game and good casual fun. Pick it up on sale and you'll be happy with your purchase.

This game is getting a lot of flak for having blocks right now. Most people will take one look at this game called "Murder Miners" and rightfully pass right over it because what, do we need another fortresscraft/minecraftclone? I implore you not to judge this game by its title or by its crafty appearance. To do so would be to deny yourself something simple and fun.
The reason this title is so cheap is not because it tries to emulate Minecraft. In fact, other than borrowing the ever-trending concept of blocks as landscape, it takes absolutely nothing else from the aforementioned survival block games. Murder Miners takes the best of the shooting genre and combines it with blocks. Its all about the fundamentals: Shooting and building.
Lets talk about shooting.
The online play is almost exclusively "guns only" meaning you won't find many people hosting a public map building session (but thats not to say you won't see them). Most servers will cater to their lobby, asking what maps they like, and what game modes.
The guns feel light and maneuverable. In short the games FPS mechanics just feel tight and classic. They offer all the weapons any decent shooter would offer, and they are simple in appearance and function. You get your Halo CE with a little bit of old timey arena shooter, and it feels great. Alot of people will say how fun the Infection mode is, and it truly is. But this isn't why the game shines the brightest in my opinion.
The thing that makes this shooter stand out from others is the "back-to-basics" mechanics that run through the whole game. It doesn't have time for the weapon attachments, the unnecessary game modes, and the hype surrounding the popular shooters of today. J force instead boils it all down to the raw, uncensored arena FPS.
The mobility offered to the player is only expanded by the use of blocks. Players can use steps of blocks (much like Faith uses steps in Mirrors Edge) to "vault" by double tapping space. This not only works with steps; any vertical surface can be jumped off of as long as you are gaining altitude, providing endless opportunities to assault your opponents.
The building is all done from a mining gun with a built-in block selection interface. You can spawn different types of blocks by selecting them with the arrow keys, and you can place them in four different ways (Line, face, float and fill). The build mechanics are primitive, but there is SO much you can do with primitive. The more fundamental the mechanics are, the more possibilities exist. One look at the workshop is enough to prove that.
All in all, the game plays very well, despite the low production value (which will show, believe me). If you like getting your guns on, but have a mind for creativity as well, this game is a great option, and the price of $1.99 is pretty attractive too.

Yet, it seems that Sang-Froid is not as rewarding for players who carefully plan out their defenses as it should be, because with careful placement of traps and minimum involvement in combat, I was constantly out of money and struggled to get the best equipment in the first half of the game. Only after few chapters, did I discover that I could just buy potions and kill enemies, thus saving money for the equipment. And that's a shame, because I would rather be rewarded for playing smart instead of casual. This aspect of the game is also illustrated by the fact that the character gains experience both for succeeding and failing the missions, which allows to unlock new skills either way, thus becoming stronger. It means that you can just grind through stat boosts, save money for better weapons and almost forget about trap placement in the first part of the game.

You wake up on a small pier facing murky waters with no recollection of who you are, you're soon approached by a ferryman and board his ship only to find out things are not as real as they seem.
A very short and simple game with a great narrative dealing with death, choices and consequences Port of Call does suffer from overly low production values but thankfully they don't detract too much from its excellent story.
-eerie, creepy atmosphere
-great story
-interesting, cryptic dialogue slowly lets you realize what's happened to you
-the music is pretty good
-while I can forgive the simple graphics I have to mention two bad elements to them: firstly most objects have a very thick black outline as a sort of faux cell shading, it doesn't really work and looks bad while also being sometimes drawn as you move making it look very unrealistic. The second problem is the quite huge amount of clipping the character models have with arms passing through themselves and pieces of skin coming out of clothes.
-very short, expect around 20 minutes to complete
-apart from a dual choice at the ending the game is very linear and has no replay value once you're done
Port of Call is basically a slightly interactive story, you move around the ship, do a few simple tasks, have conversations with people you meet (sometimes choosing between a few different questions) and that's that: its story is truly great though and makes the game a worthwhile experience. I cannot spoil anything but while starting a bit slow and murky you'll eventually hit a twist that explains everything and have to face a decision that truly has some emotional strings attached to it.
The game is an easy recommendation to anyone wanting to experience a good story, it made me wish the devs had an higher budget to truly flesh it out and make a complete game out of it: even as things stand you'd play it at least once and, to be honest, a second playthrough to see the other ending while reading again through conversations knowing what truly happened is also is totally worth it.

In some western cultures during Christmas, Santa sneaks into peoples' homes and leaves presents to the nice children. Why he has to sneak like that? Why not just boldly step into their homes and be warmly welcomed? Well, that's just the weird Finnish way.
Anyhow, this becomes the idea behind
. Children and sometimes adults are on the look out to catch
while he sneaks to the Christmas tree, leaves his gifts and sneaks back to the chimney.
Each level starts and ends at the chimney. Santa has to find his way to the Christmas tree while avoiding any "guards" like children, gun-wielding elderly and dogs, and traps like bear traps and effing mines and lasers. Santa gets three doses of sleep powder to take out guards to add some tactics to the party.
Bonus points (and an achievement) can be got by also feasting on all the cookies and eggnog you can find, usually hiding behind an additional set of traps and guards.
As a funny detail, the levels are children on "Nice lists" and "Naughty lists" etc. Nice people's houses are (quite logically) the easy levels and the naughtier they get, the more traps and guards there are. Also, as a nice detail the naughty children surely don't get presents. Finally, you even get to play as Krampus, with his own powers!
In a way the easy and medium levels act as organic tutorials, introducing new mechanics and traps. The level design is good and diverse. Everything is deterministic, if not always synchronized, rendering the levels into kind of stealth puzzles, especially once the freaking murderers appear.
While the game is good, its options are limited. The controls are arrow keys and space (for action) but they cannot be changed. There appears to be no controller support currently. Aspect ratio can be changed conveniently at any time but otherwise there are no resolution options or option to go windowed mode or adjust volume settings.
As for gameplay, my only qualm are the clumsy, unreliable hitboxes. The game appears to use two different kinds of hitboxes, ones for stationary traps and ones for guards with sight. The stationary traps were okay: you hit the trap if your shadow directly under you hits it so that's logical.
However the guards, with their various lines of sight, would sometimes notice Santa even just seeing a tip of his hat. I felt it didn't make sense much as it surely looked like they wouldn't notice him. It could be even rage-inducing at times to lose a level repeatedly through such shenanigans.
A word on the music, I'm sure you are not surprised that it's a bunch of remixed Christmas tunes. A pleasant soundtrack, it's not fancy but it works.

I'm not usually one to play the point and click adventure genre, but this one sucked me in early. The story and voice acting are actually really good, and I played all the way through. When the credits started to roll I found out why it wasn't a terrible, terrible game: The dialogue was written by Orson Scott Card, and the story partially came from Stephen Speilberg, back when he was awesome. Anyways, you should play it.

So a friend recommended this to me. After barely an hour, I can't imagine why.
It even starts in the menu where you can't control the menu with the D-pad which is something I'd expect. Options are the bare minimum you'd come to expect for a PC game and volume levels are incredibly clunky to adjust unless you're using a controller -- there are no proper sliders. The volume adjustments don't carry on to the cutscenes either, so while listening to audiobooks, music or anything along those lines you should expect interruptions by LOUD NOISES, often in the shape of horrible dialogue (not that I would ever play this for the story).
When the game isn't playing itself and taking away the controls from you, it plays like crap. Some actions feel very mechanical and like you're locked in (wall-running, for example) and any precis platforming is pretty much impossible since Sonic slides around way more than you'd expect.
Also, for a game that's about high speeds you're forced to a sudden stop by sudden walls. If you try to keep momentum by jumping over them, you'll lost it and any speedy sections will last for a total of five inches before something stops you.
I'm not big into Sonic and if this is among the best the franchise has to offer, I can clearly see why.

Personally, I didn't like how your ship is moved by clicking on the map for your desination, and the fact the ship auto-fires when you click on an enemy is just boring for me.
But hey, if you like the story to be a tutorial, and you don't mind only using your mouse to control your ship... then try out this game it looks polished and it may be a fun experience for you.

Amazing! The gameplay was very well done, and finishing some of the levels made me feel like a genius!
The story was surprisingly well written. Doing the dirty work of 4 opposing sides is just a generally good concept. And the writers understood how to make you project on to your character. Rather than going the silent protaganist route, they gave you dialog options that allow you to choose between being a badass cop, or a sassy detective. The ending kinda sucked though. I was expecting a huge climax at the end, but it was just kind of half baked. I would have loved if they worked in a plot twist. I know there are multiple endings, but I kind of wish that they had put thought into both of them. The story is kind of hard to keep up with at times, but after reading a few old text messages, I got it completely. The dialouge is funny too.
The gameplay is somewhat generous. And what I mean by that is; there are a lot of achievements. Like...a lot.
The best part of the gameplay is that there are no pre set solutions. You come up with the answer yourself, making it both a strategy game and a puzzel game, which gives it infinite replay value. The levels are hard, but not to the point where I wanted to give up and go punch a brick. I'm not saying that I liked it because it was easier than most puzzel games, but it was refreshing to have a nice relaxing time killer, where getting frustrated isn't very common. That's not to say it's casual. It's surprisingly not casual at all.
Overall, the amount of thought put into the story, and the incredibly fun gameplay make for a gaming expirience that I will never stop replaying.

An adventure in the classic point-and-click vein. These live or die on two things: the strengths of their story and puzzles. This game carries both.
The story would fit right in as a sci-fi blockbuster: a team on a mission to save the earth from an asteroid discovers it's actually a ship, and get stranded on a deserted planet. And that's just the first 10 minutes. Time to explore the ruins and get back home. Includes the usual sci-fi commentary on the hazards of the pursuit of certain goals -- I'm trying to stay spoiler-free, but you'll understand as you find & use the green crystals.
The puzzles are difficult but not unfair. (These days you have online walkthroughs, but where's the fun in that?) There's the usual inventory-combination tricks, but there are also environmental puzzles like operating the controls of a crane with the input of a series of colors, each of which performs a certain movement.
Graphics are a little dated in HD times, but don't let that stop you.

Sonic Lost World is a very entertaining Sonic game, in my opinion, and offers a lot that many don't even stick around to witness. For one, the graphics are amazing. (Max them out if your PC can handle it, you will be impressed) The levels are colorful, vibrant, and are very unique; as this is a port of the Wii-U Version, a lot of... out of place (?) levels will be seen. Such as one full of nothing but candy, giving impressions that Sonic is very HIGH. But unique is what we remember, and what we will love.
But graphical beauty is only the beginning! Design was a big step as well (Super Mario Galaxy step, yes, but I think they wanted to bring in Nintendo fans with their contract with them) You can go up-side down, climb up walls, double-jump (Yeah! That's right!) and of course the best of all, the return of the beloved Spin-Dash! Classic styles of gameplay make a return, and it actually works. Except... they did screw one thing up. Sonic has a run button. I know... it's bad, but it does find it's perks if you are using the keyboard instead of a controller. But either control set, this game is fairly easy. The bosses are fun, although unintimidating (Excluding Zavok) and bring good comical value to the game.
"The Deadly Six" they are called, and are controlled by Eggman with the power of a special conch he obtains, until... well, I won't spoil it! But it's basically Sonic and Tails the whole time. You DO see Amy and Knuckles for maybe 3 minutes all-together, but that's all. Kinda' sad no extra characters come. But I highly reccommend this game to Sonic fans or anyone else. It is a great platformer that shouldn't be hated just because it took a different route!

At first, I was really excited to try this game out since it is kinda like Portal 2 and the developers said that it was a whole new experience.

This new element is manipulating the bounce and speed gels found in Portal 2. I actually liked this new concept.
I found the first few minutes of the game really gluggy and slow and that boat scene though but after the first chapter things sped up a bit, literally. As I haven't played the full game, on purpose, I can safely say, at least type, that I actually want to finish the game. It's brought a new idea to the table and I give the developers credit for that.
My two concerns for this game are that one of the opening scenes, the boat one, it seemed like the player was rapidly jumping up and down. The other is that all the signs are identical to each other, such as the gel flow signs have gel crossed and stuff writen next to it in the exact same way for all the posters. The creators could have put a bit of originality to the game and made the signs different.
Many people think that Nigel, the 'Wheatly' of this game, has bad voice acting but I believe that's why the creators called him Nigel.
I actually want to play this game to the end. It's really good considering its <$10 even though you need to have Portal 2 installed to play it. So all up I reckon $30- is a great price for an extrodinary game created by Valve and a new concept to go along with it.

Sure it has a Pay wall but that is how it has survived throughout the years and it encourages players to continue playing in order to get the most out of breeching the pay wall rather than the true free to play/free to win model where you reach the end and that's it.
I also like to tout that your decisions matter, the economy in this game is strictly player run with the exception of a few instances in the game's history where a billion ISK (Inter stellar Kredit) ship was dropped below 500 million, if you sell stuff to an alliance at war you may tilt the outcome to where one or more sides comes out victorious.
Pros:
-Decisions matter
-PvP everywhere
-Longevity
-Beautiful ships
Cons:
-Dated User Interface
-Tutorial needs more explanation to keep new players

The Dig was originally planned to be a major motion picture by Steven Spielburg, but he decided that special effects were not at a sufficent level to bring justice to the visuals he wanted to achieve.
So instead he turned to his good friend George Lucas to have his talented staff at Lucasarts turn the script into a game.
The result is one of the most cinematic adventure games of all time. It invokes feelings of wonder and awe, of horror and amazement. The scope of the game both encompasses the grandiose exploration of a world never seen by man, and the personal trials of the wonderfuly-realized characters who find themselves stranded there.
This game is a personal favorite of mine, and I'm very glad that it's available on Steam for others to experience it. It's only $5, for goodness' sake.

This game is not as dead as one may think. Sure, the peak player count per day is not very high, but recently a few of the old devs have come out of the shadows to say 'I want this game done.' and they have taken to the community to help them finish it. With programs like ITO which will allow players to play-test new updates that will be coming out and a brand new, playerbase-driven dev team? This game will be able to do anything. The game hasn't been updated much in 4 years, but when I recently came back to it in the Community discord with like 10-12 people in game with me, we all had a blast!
The core concept of the game as of right now is story-driven updating. The game is currently in early access, therefore the players (or Marines) who have this game are in a 'training' phase of sorts. When the game fully releases the Marines will be sent on actual operations to combat an actual enemy amongst the stars. But for right now, we are located in a training facility beneath Nevada, honing our skills to become the best Marine we can be.
Operations wise, the game has a few really good ones that just ooze with lore. The Neurogen Incident for instance is a recreation of an actual event that happened in the Neurogen facility located above Earth, a bio-hazardous toxin was released and caused a lot of the people inside of the facility to become 'zombies' which is simulated by the unarmed CTRs (Combat Training Robots) that run at you screaming in an attempt to not only scare the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you but also kill you. In this mission, it is very dark and the atmosphere of this destroyed space-station just gives you the creeps all over. The announcer even tells you, 'if fear of the dark and the unknown is something that affects you, it is best to abort this mission now.' This is just one of the operations that you can go on, and it takes a good 20 minutes to complete it depending on your speed.
Then you have Multiplayer and Wargames, wargames being a sort of 'survival' situation where you are thrown into a random environment with nothing but your wits and a pistol against CTRs that almost always aim for the head. You need to use stealth and be aware of your environment in order to survive.
Multiplayer is teams vs teams and it is sooo much fun, I had a blast playing with one of the devs last night and got to laugh pretty hard when I managed to kill him once or twice, and of course having a dev there to go through the issues the game might be facing right now is pretty cool. It was sort've funny, whenever we encountered a problem we would say something like 'take notes, man!'
Overall I love this game, and I'm going to keep giving it my support, I hope to be able to purchase the Spearhead edition soon. If you want to play this game, and you are looking for people to play with, go to this discord -
and find some people! We don't exactly have people constantly playing but it's still a good opportunity to find some people who also play the game.

EVE Online is best played with people, which is probably why it's called EVE Online instead of EVE Offline. This game should be fantastic! It's got crazy colourful worlds, a kicking soundtrack, some neat boss concepts and a cool Mario Galaxy/Sonic Xtreme twist to the level design.
But, in true Sonic fashion, the problem lies in the excecution. Sonic's new controls are an unholy mishmash of the previous 3D games with a bunch of Assasin's Creed thrown in, and they are
. Moves fail when they shouldn't, your speed and direction never feel like they match your inputs, that parkour is too sticky whenever it shouldn't be (and vice-versa) and otherwise clever movement tweaks like ice skating, rail grinding and a snowball thing feel even more half-baked. Previous 3D Sonics had some bad,
controls, but they were consistent in their awfulness; they could be
. Lost World's inconsistent control mess is almost untameable, and they fail some enjoyable level design.
There's also a plot that could fit on the back of a small napkin, stretched far past the breaking point. Almost every level has a cutscene, and the vast majority of them don't need to exist. The cameo villians have no character (yet demand most of the story's attention) and a bizzare serious tone pervades an otherwise silly adventure. Despite my low hours counter, I have played this game again and again before it was on Steam.
That said, Galatic Battlegrounds is a underappreciated jewel in the RTS genre. It runs on the same engine as Age of Empires 2 - and even take many inspirations from it - but have a very different playstyle.
First of all, you will be playing the major factions in the Star Wars Saga instead of medieval civs. Many of the factions were showed much on the films, so this game is a nice chance to see more of the universe (the Gugans, for instance).
Second, the campaigns are cool. They obviously aren't cannon, but they talk about very specific moments of the Star Wars universe (again, the Gugans one follow the events that lead to the unification of the gugan tribes). Some of them even share a same storyline and characters, like the Rebel Alliance and Republic.
Third, the proper gameplay. Galatic Battlegrounds is a lot more fast paced combat then Age of Empires 2. It features all the same unit archetypes as Ao2, plus Aerial combat and Invisible units. A very distint change from one game to another is the presence of more "Hard-Counters". Meanwhile Ao2 uses a "Soft-Counter" style (a Knight can kill some Pikemen before dying; the cost-effiency favors the Pikemen but the Knight can do something), Galatic Battlegrounds' "Hard-Counter" means that when a unit is paired against its counter it has a much less usefulness and can become almost useless.
This paired with the much easier economy can favor some fast-paced games with intense tech-switching .

What I imagine going through the guards' head all the time
"Oh look that soldier/civilian/wanted man running at super-human speed/running on the wall/flying above us! Must be my imagination."
"The virus scanner went crazy every time that soldier walked by. Must be malfunctioning."
"There was five of us ten seconds ago and now there's only two of us here. Everything is fine, carry on."
"I saw Jenkins consumed by an infected not too long ago, and there he is back in the base. He must've get better."
By the time I done with this game I reckon the average IQ for the area increased by at least 50 points.

For the Younger Crowd
I've been playing games a long time, and while the younger crowd might enjoy their experience it was nothing new to me.  The premise is nothing I haven't seen before and while the explanation for the shadows is good, it's not like the game brings anything fresh.
I realize it's an experiment, but for the content presented there needs to be more than what's given.  This is the sort of thing that would be better suited to a different format because the simple graphics fail to make it all that imersive.  Nobody seems to mind me bouncing books or other items off them, I could see where the story was going after meeting the little old man (and confirmed by the time I met the little girl) that there was really no surprises for me.
I'd recommend a different engine.  The first person view just doesn't work for the amount of abstraction the game clearly wants to capture.  The story is far too short, too linear, and too straightforward.  The concept isn't bad but it needs a different presentation -- otherwise it's just another walking around sim.

It's an action trap-defense game, sort of similar to Orcs Must Die, but much more tense and thrilling (as opposed to the wacky, over-the-top Orcs Must Die). Each trap is costly to place, so strategy is paramount. Game provides clear information about enemy movement, so any time a trap fails, you know that fault lies with you. The action part of it involves you running in the dark snowy winter, trying to take out the few (were)wolves who have evaded your traps.
At least 2 or 3 playthroughs can be very rewarding because of the variety of ways to build your character. By varying the build, you can nudge the gameplay either towards more trap-strategy, or more running and shooting. I personally love the trap + sniper skill build.
Downside: Bad voice-acting. Just ignore it. Story is decent, but cutscenes are clunky.
Overall, great tense game with a good mix of strategy and action. New mechanics and enemies keep every level fresh, while different builds provide replayability.

There's things about this game that I like and there's things that I don't however overal, I'd have to give it a thumbs down. To start this off, I'll start with the pros (what's good) of the game and then I'll get to the cons (what's bad).
First off, the soundtrack is amazing. It's original and well done, there's not much more I could say about it. The game was fun at times although it certainly wasn't anything like Portal and I did like the idea of just testing with gels. Honestly my favorite part of the game was when I was testing in test chambers that were in Portal 2 meant for the portal gun instead of the paintgun. However it was a very short segment and was considered no time compared to all the custom test chambers the delevopers made. Personally, I would've liked to see more of this but I can't speak for the rest of Portal fans who were also disappointed to play this game. There's also a part where you're time and you have to go really fast. I attempted five or four times before becoming furstrated with the game (I'm horrible at timed games, it's too much stress). However what I didn't notice was that the developers were nice enough to have a button to skip it. I know there was probably a lot of effort placed into this game and I feel so sorry for siding with everyone who dislikes this game but there's just too many flaws.
Now to what's wrong with the game. I have to begin with all the broken test chambers. There's a lot of bugs and glitches in this game and for some reason my game hit pretty much all of them. There was a part where I was supposed to jump to a certain point with repulision gel but no matter what I ended up jumping either too high or too low and dying. This was never a problem when I played Portal 2. I ended up looking up a walkthrough and it showed everything that I was doing yet somehow the person got to the place the jump was supposed to get them. Another glitch I had was that in a level that needed propulsion gel, the gun wouldn't activate it for some odd reason (I once again looked online to find that I was doing everything right). For both levels, I was forced to use console because there was no other way to get through them. Another thing wrong was the aim in the game. The cross hair was a lot higher than where the gun would actually fire and it made me want to pull my hair out. Throughout the game, you're with a core named Nigel. At first I thought Nigel was kinda cute and funny but after awhile I began to realize how much I couldn't stand him. He was just so whiny (which at first was funny) and wouldn't stop talking. Another part about Nigel that I didn't like was that he wouldn't let you start certain tests until he was done talking (which sometimes felt like forever). In much later test chambers, Nigel would follow you around on a rail (I really don't remember what its called) like Wheatley from Portal 2 but to me this was a huge distraction. I disliked trying to solve a test chamber and having my eyes be confused by Nigel's rail, mistaking it for something that was part of the test chamber. The game also had next to no plot. There's no way that I could cause spoilers because there's no plot. You do test chambers with a core named Nigel and that's about it. It seems to me that this is a really dull portal fanfiction placed last second instead of just having the players go through test chambers. As a really big fan of portal (a person next to obsessed with it) I noticed several things wrong. For example, the first few test chambers look alike to those of Cave Johnson's (in fact I swear I saw the old Aperture logo somewhere) which is confusing because there's not really a reason to. What bothered me more is how much later test chambers had weird and very distracting backgrounds. I might be nitpicking here but personally it bothered me to no end. I forgot to meantion the worst part of this game. The autosaving is terrible. You could have been half way done with the map and lose everything (which is honestly fine, people need to save more often) but what was worse was when it autosaved me at broken points. The game has autosaved while I was failing a jump and about to die (several test chambers this happened to me), causing me to have to load an ealier save. The last and probably biggest point is that I paid four dollars (which is now seven dollars) for a game that has too many problems and isn't even a stand alone game. I don't want my money back but I still don't think that this should cost unless the majority of the problems are fixed.
I have yet to play the Steam community's levels yet I'm not reinstalling this game anytime soon.
This is all just my opinion, feel free to disagree. Though I'll finish this up by saying that this actually gets more hate than it really deserves.

I'm still waiting to see where this game goes, but as of today I unfortunately cannot recommend this.
Unfortunate negatives:
The game's development team has dwindled down as this project has lost its funding over the years and I fear the existing team is misguided with what they're focusing efforts on currently.  The last major content update I remember the game getting was something called Wargames- it's a scheduled event that occurs a couple times a week and is effectively a battle royale. That's the only real multiplayer this has outside of co-op missions (which are polished but very barebones and, frankly, boring) and I've never been able to play due to how it's scheduled and not on-demand.  This was a horrible return on investment if you ask me.
If you look at the Trello page the developers currently seem to be working on nothing other than performance and graphics improvements, bug fixes, and...character skins?   A recent dev post mentions how they're working on a Unity 5.6 upgrade making things "prettier"...these are things that should be done towards the end of a game's development cycle, not when the game is barely clinging to life by the efforts of a handful of devs including volunteers.  Where is the additional content?  Where are the enemies, weapons, and game modes?  Where is the equipment?  Where are the *features*?
Positives:
I will say that what little content is here is in pristine condition.  In the 12 hours I've played in the past couple years I never once encountered a bug between myself and my friends (making the current dev priorities even more perplexing...) and every single feature felt well-implemented.  Guns have good feedback, sound effects are incredible across the board, visuals are great, player HUD is well-implemented and immersive, difficulty is good, netcode is reliable, etc.  The game is of high quality.
Conclusion:
The game desperately needs content and it seems the devs are prioritizing the wrong things, but when Zero Point develops a feature they do it right and I have to credit them for emphasizing quality.

I can't believe I'm saying this, but I would totally recommend this game. I finished the game and I love it. But let me explain, I didn't love it all along the way.
The opening 3D worlds of this game are gems. Levels done right. Designed for fast movement and collecting rings. Exactly what makes Sonic great. So many people complain about the addition of a run button, but this is a feature I've felt necessary in Sonic games for years. Yes, Sonic is meant to move fast, but without being able to properly control his momentum, he can easily go TOO fast.
As the game went on, the 3D levels became a little more generic. Was that a bad thing? Not necessarily. I still enjoyed them.
What my gripe with this game comes from is the 2D levels. Every one of them was frustrating and slow and even downright unfair at times. I found myself rage quitting only these levels. However, even when they're all of the things mentioned above, I still had fun doing it.
The bosses are generic and cliche but I found them interesting and funny, still. I enjoyed encounters with them and their dialogue felt like good old one liner back and forths from Adventure.
But does this make sense? At all? I found myself complaining about how much I didn't like the game during those 2D  sections or whenever I got frustrated with anything else, only to finish the game and find that I'm absolutely in love with it. How does that happen? This game is extremely special. It's a game that splits Sonic fans. If they were to continue in this direction, (but either eliminate or fix those damn awful 2D sections) then I would be totally content. Sonic has finally reached a point where he can be controlled the right way and his games are playable and enjoyable.
The only thing this game really needed was a hub world rather than the map screen, which was a bit disappointing, but fun nonetheless. I recommend this game highly. Somehow.

It's not a "mining" or "survival sandbox" game by any means. You're shooting other players in a competitive enviornment. The only similarity this game has to minecraft (and I honestly dislike that it  can even be compared to minecraft) is that you build the maps with blocks. That's it. Secondly, you need to know that this game moves and shoots exactly like a Halo game, with the exception that you can do some wall kicks and other moves like that. Anyways, the last thing you should know is that this game still needs more polish in the graphics and presentation departments. You'll probably be able to do the same! I'd be sure to hop on this game quickly, because Jforce plans to add a lot to it. These devs have a lot of good ideas for the game. Well, that's all I've got.

I've been into this game on xbox hardcore since February 2013. Murder Miners. They say it's halo and minecraft. I say that is not the case. You can expect blocks, sure, sure. But that is where the minecraft aspect ends.
The gameplay is of course, is very much like Halo CE, with the twelve shot magnum, the four shot snipers, motion sensors, and the shields, the players armor, but there's more than that. You have WAY more mobility than in any halo game I have seen. You can sprint, dodge, double jump(more like wall scaling) and 'ram' attack, a special movement option players get in versus modes. they look down while sprinting, increasing their movement speed, and become a deadly walking projectile. So why is this Halo and Minecraft?
Halo and Minecraft? No. no, no, no, and no. First, there is no survival concept whatsoever. No food, no home to build before night, and no open world three times the size of earth. There is Forge/ Creative mode, no doubt, but it is not halo and minecraft.
My description of Murder Miners would be Halo gameplay hybridized with Unreal Tournament,(Look that game up on here, its pretty sick!) due to the high player mobility, arena maps, and weapon balancing, with a pinch of minecraft blocks.
As I'm sure what many of you want to know, how is the infection? I'd say it's probably the best infection you can possibly find in any game, and yes it's 10 times better than halo. In fact, it makes halo infecton look like someone took a giant pile of crap, and combined it with another pile of crap and placed it in a microwave for 10 minutes. Disgusting. As a Zombie, you can tongue grapple, activate radar, and level up by consuming the corpses of the freshly dead. This awesome ability makes you faster and stronger, and your abilities become more efficient. And your levels stick with you after death! It is the first game where I truly had fun playing as zombie.
To me, this game was a divine gift from the heavens. I believe that if you love halo, but know that the series won't be getting better any time soon, you need this in your library. It's fun with friends, it's competitive, it has a lot of content for what the devs are charging, so get it asap!

Son Goku? Wrong! A character you create from the ground up. Either a sayin, a humam, a majin, a frieza, or a namekian. The second problem: The Customization. Everything is so bland, your basically making a character from leftovers of other characters from the show. Your character is a lookalike of some chracter from Dragon Ball if you choose a human or a sayin. You get some cool custom options as any of the other species (I love playing as a Frieza). The story for this game is pretty easily explained. You basically fix all the arcs in the DBZ timeline, you unlock skills and outfits for your character through parallell quests to get stronger. It's not bad but it's a lot of work to find out the final boss is something completely irrelevant. The Combat: It feels like DBZ. Which is a good thing. You have four slots for basic attacks: Combos, Ki Blasts, Transformations, all things you've seen from the show. And your ultimate moves where you whip out when your ki is full and you want to just devastate your foes. However there is a limit to what you can do in the game. There are three modes, campaign, parrellel quests where you'll spend most of your time and battles. Can you go Super Sayin? Yes you can, Super Sayin 2? You bet. Ultimate 1 and 2. Hell yeah. But the transformations end there. If your not a sayin you will be limited to KaiokenX20 even with the DLC. I wanted to be able to become Super Sayin God and Super Sayin God Super Sayin. With the Ressurection of F pack you don't get that or Golden Frieza transformations for your character you made. You don't get Super Sayin 4 either from the GT packs which is really disappointing. Murder Miners is a game about fast reactions, equal combat, and zombie warfare. In Zombie Survival, Co-op is VITAL. Zombies are fierce, and you must act fast. But take a second too long, and you're food-unless your buddy behind you makes a clean kill! When given the chance, build up defenses with the Miner Gun to extend your chance of action! Occasionally, a dead zombie drops small amounts of ammo, so loot when given the opportunity! Free-for-all mode makes you use your brain a bit more. With the speed and agility, you and your enemies will be dashing corners and bouncing off walls here and there. Keep that triggerfinger ready for anything! Team Murdermatch is a different story. Vehicles are strong when every seat is being used, so you need to make a big enough force to startle your enemy and go from defense to offense. Or take to the borderlines and give sniper support to your team as they advance throughout the map. In Murder the Flag, Things get hectic. Because the combat is pretty brutal and quick, you and your team need to be vigilant. You never know what the enemy is doing. That is why you must keep the flag gaurded securly, while a strike team goes to the enemy base and snags the flag. Good luck getting home in one piece. Last but not least, is the horror show of infection. One player starts as a zombie, with the optional help of other Zombie AI. This player must go and kill other humans. Using their tounge to bring the survivor to them, or bloody claws to shred both flesh and construction, the zombies will easily breach the humans line of defense! One by one, the humans will be picked off by the speedy undead. Humans, watch the bodies of the fallen survivors. Zombie players have the chance to eat the dead survivor and evolve traits. Do whatever it takes to halt the zombies, or they will get stronger and stronger before you see it coming! Once you have esperienced the chaos and want to relax, you might want to head over to Map-Making Mode.This is where you create your blocky battlefield.
I have introduced Murder Miners to many of my friends, in which they all thought the game was really fun. If you ask me, you should grab this game and have a game night with all your buddies on a Friday night!

There are probably too many games that take place in America to count nowadays, sometimes having it be just a setting, others making silly or outlandish portrayals of what life in the US of A is like. But that means other countries don't appear as often, particularly their neighbour to the north and my home country, Canada. Heck, we don't even have our own hero in Overwatch yet! So I was interested in playing Sang-Froid, since I heard it described a bunch in this thread as just about the most Canadian thing ever. Is it?
Well, the story goes like this: it's Klondike-era Canada, and lumberjack Joseph and his sister Josephine have been run out of their town thanks to the priest blaming the local church burning down on her. This forces them to shack up with their brother Jacques, who Joseph is none-too fond of, and the feeling is mutual. There's not much time to think about that, though, as it turns out this priest has been bewitched by the Devil, who is corrupting the townspeople into werewolves and sending them to try and spirit their sister away for unknown reasons. Since they both care for her more than they dislike the other, it's time to kill some werewolves.
Much like Orcs Must Die, you participate in the defense firsthand. You can play as either Joseph, who is quite physically fit and capable of fighting off enemies better, or Jacques, who is more of a hard mode where you need to rely on traps. Of course, the extensive skill tree is the same for both, as is most of the story, save some scenes where they're alone. It's probably inaccurate to compare this to Orcs Must Die, though, as Sang-Froid is more slow-paced and strategic.
The story takes place from the fifth of December all the way to Christmas Eve, and as each day dawns you're able to go to town to buy items, equip your character, and of course lay traps for the werewolves at night. Each level has three waves, with the enemies in them almost always going for different targets; you'll have up to five buildings to defend by the end of the game. Thankfully just clicking on an enemy's icon will show you the exact path they'll take once they show up, barring distractions.
If that sounds a bit easy, it isn't, as your arsenal is nowhere near autonomous. The only no frills weapon you have is the starting bear trap, which will kill a common wolf, but barely slow a werewolf down without picking skills to power it up. Most others you have to activate yourself or have some requirement before they'll trigger, like a net you need to shoot down with your rifle (which, being a nineteenth century firearm, you'd better not miss with), or a spike trap that will only trigger if three enemies are on it at once, which often requires luring them with bait or your scent. Engaging enemies yourself is tricky too, since there's a stamina system in place to keep you from swinging mindlessly, and most of them have a resistance to ordinary weapons; you'll need to pay to have them blessed if you want to get around that.
All this means you generally need to go through the waves and prepare traps for each set of enemies, perhaps deciding which you can deal with yourself safely. The next wave doesn't come until everything from the previous one is dead, and it gives you enough time to move across the map if you need to, especially later on when you unlock watch-towers you can zipline between. If you screw up, the game lets you restart at either dawn, to place traps differently, or at twilight, if you made some misstep in execution. It's definitely not the kind of game where you can sit and watch as things march to their doom, but there was something about setting things up and watching - or listening - to it all go right.
I beat the game in nine hour as Joseph, and enjoyed myself a lot more than I expected going in. I'd say it's a bit of a hidden gem, although it has been on sale quite a lot at this point. I'd thoroughly recommend it so long as Canadian accents don't make you recoil in horror. Last I checked the developers were still planning on making a part two to the game, and I hope they do if it's as good.

So, I refuse to play the game.
However, EVE online's negative aspects go further than this; for instance, in terms of an immersive experience, there are much better games on the market (such as Elite Dangerous) which feature better graphics, UI Systems, and controls than this does. It's just a shame their customer service is even slower.

A Stand Alone Mod for half life 2. Its very well done, even though the actual game itself is is good, not great, which is why i gave it a 6.
The Pros:
Atmosphere: Surprisingly well done in the atmosphere department. I liked it
Gameplay: Plays like half life 2 so yeah you know its gonna be good
Voice Acting: it was good, alot better than I had anticipated, well done!
Pacing: I thought the game went along pretty well on the path that it wanted you to go on.
The cons:
Enemies: Really boring zombie-like enemies that are super easy to kill
Weapons: its been a bit since i've played this game, but if i remember correctly you could only carry one weapon at a time. I did not like that , i felt 2 would have been more adequate.
Story: while i enjoyed the story to an extent, i felt it left to many unanswered questions. But seeing as how this is only the first part in a series, it can be overlooked, just dont expect any real explanation or closure for the story.
In conclusion, do i recommend this game? Hell yes I do. For one thing it's free, and it's well done. So knock yourself out with Estranged Act 1.

Perhaps the worst coded game I have played. The initial install will provide a broken or corrupt start icon so go into the directory and try the "NWZ Launcher" icon. From there, you will need to start Steam first, then start the game using that NWZ icon, log into Aeria manually, then retry and it works. Possible causes, too many third party software logins or errors, or the game does not pass fully through the firewall due to all these programs. There is almost no credible documentation online on how to fix it either, even from the devs. There are also some issues with lag spikes that require some adjustments, defragging files.

WOW!
While I felt the movement was a little fast at first when I went into the "Test Robot" level to run around for a few minuets to learn the basic controls I'll admit I was skeptical at the time..
It took almost 5 minuets for my first match to connect which was also disapointing but I stuck it out and I have to say it was worth the wait!
From what I saw in an hour this game is verry awesome and exciting based on my first impression. While the development team is selling in game purchesses to advance your robot.. there doesn't seem to be anything that gives a totaly unfair advantage to the player who doesn't pay out, which is really nice. Considering the team is only a small group of 6 people making this happen I'm really impressed. I'm happy such a good game is available for free, and it's not pay-to-win.
Beyond the satisfaction of experiancing fast-pased team deathmatch and area control maps the robot customization appears to be the best I've seen in any game period. If you ever played that game with all of the easily-recognizable, overly popularized corporate-funded animated characters from worlds abound.. you'll understand what I mean when I use the term Jelly-Bot. The starting robot really hinted towards an all too fimilliar giant robot battle arena setting, it's so much more than that.. REALLY! Your robots are compleetly customizable from mode of transpertaion to weapon load out, shape, size and.. even team-healing weapons (nice touch I can't wait to experiment with that!). The best part about the customization from what I saw was that it seemed to encourage creativity, rather than unlike in a lot of other similar (maybe even more popular) games which really only seem to want to restrict you.
There are as many veriaty in game modes as there are in customization as well, from ranked to unranked, customized options as well as A.I. battles.. which seemed to use other player created robots rather than some default run-of-the-mill machines.
I'm just saying, really.. I play a lot of video games, some of them come on as an obsession for a little while and leave my life as quickly as they entered it, while others stick around for years and years on my adgenda. I've been into this kind of customizational giant-robot/combat-car genre before and really only found in the end the system was entirely too limiting or straight up pay-to-win. I can assure you, this is not one of those games. I played three matched in my first hour and was awarded an epic class weapon upon my first victory, which was really exciting.
Overall I feel like this is a game made by gamers, for gamers. Infact, the only short comming I see about my experiance playing this so far is that I can't afford to donate money to the development team at this time. This, I feel wouldn't be money spent in vain.

REVIEW:
Murder Miners. Originally launched back on the Xbox Live Indie Marketplace in 2012, this title takes the best aspects of the FPS Halo (In particular, Halo: Combat Evolved) and shoves it into a Voxel Battleground, reminiscent of Minecraft.
The game just got out of a closed beta, and in it's current state is pretty much the ultimate edition of the game. For $5 (Currently $4) you get access to hundreds of maps pre-made by JForce and the community, with plenty of your favorites (I'm talking maps like Blood Gulch, pretty much every Halo map, and even Unreal Tournament 2004 maps). You do have the ability to make your own maps, with a pretty in depth map editor comapred to other titles in the genre.
Gameplay is where Murder Miners shines. The developers have fine tuned this monster to Quake 3 levels of responsiveness, leaving you with tight, fast controls. Of course, you can always lower it to suit your playstyle; Want to play like your playing Halo? Drop it down to 4. Minecraft? 3. The gunplay is great. You'll have access to 6 weapons; A Halo Battle Rifle, 3 Shot Magnum, Sniper, Energy Sword (Looks like a medieval sword), Shotgun, Machine Gun, and a Hookshot (Grappling hook). These pretty much play like you'd expect them to, and you end up with some sweet♥♥♥♥♥montage clips when using the grapple hook.
The game isn't all running around though. Take to the skies in a Helicopter style vehicle and reign death from above with heavy missles. Take 2 friends up with you to give some additional firepower from above. Or perhaps you're after a burst of speed? No problem, grab a hoverbike and get to work.
One of the BEST features of Murder Miners is the Infection Game Mode. Zombies versus Humans. The maps that you get default with this game for Infection are awesomely amazing, such as burnt out cities, military bases, all giving that erry vibe that an enemy isn't too far away. 30 people in an infection game on a big map equals lots o' fun. Plus, if you're a lonely person, you can have zombie AI bots! There's fun for everyone here!
The amount of possibilities in Murder Miners are pretty much endless, and if you're a fan of Halo you'll be drooling from nostalgia after playing this.
One of the most intriguing new game ideas I've played in a long while. It succeeded in everything it tried to do, I cannot wait for a sequel.

I have played Interstellar Marines for years. Truthfully the only thing killing this game at the moment is lack of community and negative reviews. Interstellar Marines is very much a working concept and is far from complete. However the core mechanics and gameplay are unique and refreshing to the otherwise tired FPS genre. It is rare for shooters to have the kind of dynamic elements that make Interstellar Marines an enjoyable experience. No two engagements are the same and the design rewards tactical play over the trademark run and gun style of modern shooters. So before you opt out of buying this game because someone with 5 or less hours says you shouldn't, consider that this game is going to be what you make of it. If you join the community, organize matches and play with friends, you're going to have a blast. If you try to lone wolf this game at this state of development, you're likely going to find yourself disappointed.

It can be a lot of fun, but it really comes down to who you are playing with. It's a social game, and the people you play with can be a mixed bag of personalities.
It's a fun casual game with a few flaws. For me at least, the enjoyment of the game comes from the people in the game with you, and the type of people who might be viewing as an audience if someone is streaming it.
As other people have mentioned, the game is best for streamers. I say this since it's a lot more fun when there is an audience voting on the winners since it adds a bit of a wild card element to it. At the same time, it's no fun when you play against a streamer with a fan base, and their audience always votes for them.
Related to streamers, some streamers need to be the center of attention, and a game can get really annoying when a streamer has to talk at all times. I've been in plenty of games where two people are up against each other but someone can't sit back and be quiet when it's not their turn, and they feel like they have to argue the cards and not let the people playing that round argue for themselves. This doesn't just apply to streamers, but I've noticed this type of behavior coming from streamers more than people who aren't streaming.
Basically, back seat gaming can get irritating when all you want to do is play your turn, but "big personalities" can't let other people play for themselves.
My other issue with the game would come down to finding people to play with. Despite the recent boost to the player base, it can still take a long time to find a game. And if you get stuck with people that are ruining your enjoyment, it can take some time to find new people to play with as you keep ending up in the same room as them.
Despite those cons, when you fight the right group of people, the game is a lot of fun and it can be a good way to meet new steam friends for other games .

Remember all those nice things I said about Prototype 1? Well this game has all of that and more.
The graphics are vastly improved. Prototype 1 looks like a PS2 game in comparison. The story isn't as good this time around though, as the plot seems very barebones and a lot of sh*t just plain doesn't make sense. I would also like to point out that I did get this feeling like the game was very "disconnected" from Prototype 1, in that it ignores or leaves behind a lot of the events that happened in the first game (for example, I don't think Elizabeth Greene is mentioned a single time). The final boss fight is amazing too a provides and adequate amount of challenge but it's worth noting that this game is overall much easier than the first. This isn't necessarily a bad thing as it makes the freeroam MUCH more enjoyable, but the campaign itself did feel a little lacking due to the lower difficulty. Also, side note, I miss Alex Mercer's voice actor from the first Prototype.
Anyway, just like the first game, Prototype 2 has fantastic sandboxing. This time around, there's 3 islands to go travel between, which includes the completely infection infested red zone. And just like Prototype 1, you can parkour around the city, murder the undead and play around with the military (you can still play "Events", but you need the Radnet DLC pack for them, which kinda sucks). One of my personal favorite things to do is go in the Red Zone and rescue hapless civilians from the streets by grabbing them and dropping them off safely at a rooftop. If you had a bad day at work, there's no better place to go than Prototype 2.
My biggest problem with the first game was that vehicles kinda killed the fun of the game. Tanks spawned like crazy around you during freeroam and strike teams were called in like nobody's business. I'm happy to say that the problem's been fixed in this one; squads of tanks no longer spawn around you while you're just trying to have some fun and strike teams are much rarer and don't get called in in quick succession anymore. Furthermore, both seem to do less damage and are much easier to take out now, thanks to weaponizing them (ripping off the minigun/rocket launcher from the vehicle) or just grabbing onto them and using a finisher (which instantly destroys the tank/helicopter). Also, with the adjusted leveling system, as well as the introduction of mutations, you can truly feel unstoppable as you tear through enemy after enemy with your arsenal of biological abilities.
With all that in mind, I think it goes without saying that Prototype 2 blows Prototype 1 out of the water in the spot for the ultimate bad*ss simulator.
One last thing, I noticed a lot of people with AMD graphics cards are having issues with the game. I myself use NVIDIA so the problems are irrelevant to me but I feel I should still point out that people running games on an AMD should be careful and do some research before buying this game. Most of the negative reviews for Prototype 2, after all, are people who can't even get the game to run or start properly.

Prototype 2 at first was hard to really give an opinion on. You play as a marine named James Heller who's basic focus is to kill his family's murderer: Alex Mercer. Heller through 3/4's of the game is a cliche 'I'm just the perfect badass' character. And it's very irritating. No, he is not very emotional past flat out angry. While the anger is understandable, it isn't acceptable to me that a character only really acts on one feeling. You will see Heller in other emotions so don't get me wrong, he isn't the same throughout the whole story (thank God). But it's only about 3 times. Other than that, he's a cocky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that can't go a minute without swearing.
As for gameplay, that's where it took me a while. The combat at first is meteocre since you have no abilities. You just mash one button. Once you get a couple abilities that's when it starts to get fun as you can use two abilities at once rather than having to switch so much in the first title. The side missions are rinsed and repeated, but you become more powerful this way and honestly, it never really gets old being able to sneak in and destroy things by morphing into another human you just "ate". They also added a timed side mission where you need to get all the intel canisters before Blackwatch gets their corrupt little hands on them. You only get two mass abilities unfortunately. The first is just the recycled devastator Mercer used. The second I don't want to spoil.
I actually like that it takes longer to unlock things in this one. You can't hijack tanks or helicopters nearly as soon as you could in the first, so it makes for more of a challenge. Overall, the gameplay is definitely better than the first, but I do miss the ability to body surf. And I also miss how you dig in and tear up the streets in the first one too. You don't really do that in this one. And if you're curious about the graphics....no they definitely are not better than the first. I run this on maximum settings and it still looks bad compared to the first. But I'm not a person to care as long as the game is solid.
As for the story, some say it's deeper than the first. Yeah I can agree with that to a point. The story is very predictable but done decent. Half of the story is told through the important people you steal memories from. I always liked that about Prototype. The end was a cliffhanger and left me wanting more. I hope at some point in the future they decide to make a Prototype 3 to either continue the story or add closure to it.
I'd say this game is worth a max of $15 to $20. Better than the first and definitely recommended. But I always feel Prototype could do so much better with the story and immersion. Lets hope they make a Prototype 3 someday and really blow our minds with it.

The only two gripes I have are only being able to carry one weapon - I suggest they up it to two. Combat is standard fair for a source engine game, but it doesn't take away anything from the game. In the beginning especially I was particularly ammo starved - sometimes running from enemies is the best way to go about.
As far as the story - it's cliche, at least based on what we're given so far, but it's well done cliche.
At the low, low price of nothing, this game is definitely worth checking out.

Warning: TL;DR
Me and Jim run for the door. Alex is swift to follow. Towards us come a hail of bullets, and I clasp my sniper firmly in my hands. The Wehrmacht are capturing buildings to make sure their attack works. Not if we can help it. This building will remain ours. Jim picks up his SMG and aims it at the corners. Me and Alex follow behind him, as our weapons aren't suited for the close quarters. I have a sniper. He, a mount-machinegun.
The explosions outside are deafening, and the enemy fire has started again. In comes a fellow american soldier with his SMG. He runs ahead of Jim in a hurry. I don't know why. He enters the next room swiftly. We hear gunfire. Then we see him fall to the ground like a puppet. We know what to do. Jim throws a grenade into the next room. We hear shouting, and then a loud explosion followed by a final scream. A german helmet lands in front of us.
Me, Jim, and Alex run up the stairs. Jim guards the stairs, just like he said he would. Alex mounts his machinegun on the windowsill, and I look through the scope and look out the window.
I see hell, as dozens of Wehrmacht soldiers storm houses and execute our fellow american soldiers. Alex can't watch anymore. Wehrmacht take cover as Alex mow them down. American soldiers still fighting in the streets, being shot by snipers from other buildings thank us, though many lose their lives because of the Wehrmacht. Only the ones taking complete cover still live. And yet, a large group of US forces enter the street from home base, half of them shot to death by the large force of Wehrmacht machinegunners and snipers.
Suddenly, Alex just falls down, and his helmet rolls of his head. Blood oozes out through his forehead. I will never forget the shock on Jim's face, and the expression on the face of the corpse.
My turn. I like through the scope and look to the windows of Nazi-occupied windows. I pass a lot of empty windows, but then I see one with a sniper. He is aiming down the scope to the streets, right at the head of an american soldier. CRACK. Fire erupts from the barrel of the sniper, and the soldier lies dead. Now the sniper is aiming at another soldier. My turn. CRACK. A bullet meets his head, and I am happy to have fired it. His helmet flies off. I now look to the streets. A group of Wehrmacht are taking cover behind the remnants of a wall, one of them being a machinegunner, firing hundreds of bullets per second. CRACK. His gun stops shooting, and while the gunner hits the ground, the group look for me. I get down to hide, but It's too late. One of them saw me, and now shouts "Scharfschütze!"
A loud BANG erupts, and the oddly loud noise of a swish hits me. I realize what happened. A german must have fired a Panzerschrek towards me. I yell at Jim to take cover, and then a rocket hits the wall next to the window. I go deaf for a moment. Then I hear German soldier yelling at eachother below me. Jim looks at me with the face he makes when he is scared. Then he looks back down the stairs.
German boots hit the ground. Sweat runs off the palms of both of us. I try telling him we need to parachute out the window, to escape, but Jim refuses. "Stick to the plan," he says. Then he starts firing.
I can tell he's having trouble with the recoil, because soon the bullets go further up, and a Nazi has a chance to aim at him and...
The Wehrmacht soldier pulls the trigger. Jim stops shooting. Jim just looks at the ground. Then a great red puddle forms beneath him. Jim is dead. Alex is dead. That american soldier we just met. Dead. I have two choices. Jump out the window, or avenge Jim (or die trying). Second option sounds appealing. I will never bow down to this tyranny. I am a soldier, and I will fight it.
I approach the stairs. I know I am going to die. I know we are going to lose this battle. But to me, that doesn't matter. I will be together with my brothers, and every day of defeat, is another chance at victory.

The best part of the game is the post game, the Hidden World. It's a world with a few mini games that are actually fun. Another great thing is the Nintendo DLC in the Wii U version. I was sad when I figured out I'd need a download code to get the NiGHTS DLC on the Wii U, but I was happy when I figured out it came with the PC version I got through the Humble Bundle. The NiGHTS DLC is the best thing in this entire game.
Another thing I found surprising about this game is how it runs. I have a really bad computer, and while I experience some lag and slow down, it worked far better than what I expected. It runs better than Generations does on this computer, which was surprising.
Overall, I'd say only get this game as a gift or in a bundle with other games. If you do get it in a bundle, give it a try. It can be a fun game at times, even if it is slow, but I can not justify paying full price for this game.
