"Sang-Froid - Tales of Werewolves" is a fusion of tower-defense, strategy and action genres, that gets all its elements
right. Set in mid 19th century in Quebec, the game is a delight to play and for the most part, is amazingly immersive. First, here is a brief about each of the three genre elements:
Pros:
-Solid mechanics, no bugs, just the right length to give a satisfying experience while being fun
-Great balance of all ingredients along with all-round balanced strategy elements
-Immersive atmosphere, all thanks to amazing folk music selection played at precisely the right pace
-Two difficullties (so slight replay value)
-Achievements are decent, they give a kind of "special" challenge, nothing gimmicky
-Responsive devs (on Steam forum, that I know of)
Cons:
-Voice acting, dialogues and cutscenes in general are the weaker points of the game; nothing game breaking but if the devs were short on cash/talent they could've forwarded the story using comic strip format (like Max Payne), narration format (like the intro video of the game) or maybe even plain written story format
-Apart from that, I just found the last 20% of the game slightly monotonous, the reasons being:
Summing up all 3 points, I think the devs could've had waves with enemies swarming in large numbers by the end levels that would force liberal cash usage and disallow you from brute-forcing it by making you impossibly outnumbered
Apart from those nitpicks, the game is really innovative and near-perfect.
Final verdict:
8.5/10, well worth the full price.

Rating: 7/10
Overview: Third Person, Tower Defense
Similar Games: Orcs must Die, Iron Brigade
The Good:
+ This games focus is more about strategy and tactics. Unlike other tower defense games that throw tons of enemies at you, SangFroid gives you less enemies but makes them more powerful. In addition, the traps you place can only be used once per level making placement even more important.
+ Lots of different traps that fit specific purposes, some must be activated manually making placement even more important.
+ Lots of different weapons and accessories for combat
+ Completing levels grants you experience to upgrade skills and traps.
+ The game does a good job of slowly introducing new enemies and traps so you never feel overwhelmed. Has a good tutorial that explains many of the games mechanics.
+ soundtrack
The Average:
Melee and range combat feels lackluster.
The Bad:
- The story deals with supernatural elements but awful dialogue and lackluster voice acting bring the entire presentation down. You could easily skip all the cutscenes and still enjoy the game
- The game is poorly optimized. Even with a computer that well exceeds the max requirements, the game had terrible frame rates. Setting a lot of the graphical option to low helped fix the problem.
- long loading time when first starting game
- For a game in this genre, this game is missing a lot of modes that are practically standard in other tower defense games. For starters, you cannot replay a level without losing all your save progress after that point. After completing the game there is very little reason to go back and play the game other than hunting for achievements.
Conclusion
A great take on the tower defense genre and has a lot of potential. I would love to see a sequel that improves a lot of its flaws.

Dead Island is probably one of the few games that I will go consistently back to as the years go by and has solidified its place as my 3rd favorite game ever created.
Table of Contents:
1. Opening and Positive Graphics
2. Positive Gameplay
3. Postive Plot
4. Negatives and Conclusion
I love this, game and have put in the hours to show as much. Graphically i think it is still relatively crisp despite its age and I cant think of too many issues with it in it a graphical sense compared to modern AAA games. That is not to say the graphics are perfect, far from it, the landscape in particular are a bit rough at time. The objects of the environment are repeated and primarly contains grass, concrete, and the same set of boulders are repeated to form mountains and boulders.
I think the aesthetics of the game make it last longer than some of its competitors, its a rather simple but interesting contrast between bright+colorful and dark+gritty. This contrast is most notable in the resort, the zombies in Dead Island do not shy away form a gore and mangled design, while the backdrop and objects in this area are bright and "exciting" with bright blue waters, lush greenery, white/beige beaches, and emphasis on the colour red of objects. Although this indepth analysis of the aesthetical choices are limited to the first environment, the structure and design choices cross into the other areas. Although the contrast is not the same as the zombies do not drastically change design from each area(although there are differences), there is not very often that there is a breach from the aesthetic feel due to the design choices in the environment and the zombies for each area.
However graphics are but one aspect to the game, the gameplay is the meat of a game. Here in my opinion is where Dead Island shines above the crowds from the individual genres that culminates into this truly unique game. From my personal video game playing and video game "research" (ie lets-plays, speedruns, trailers, etc), Dead Island is the best zombie sandbox, hands down. The firearms in Dead Island are nothing to write home about unless you mod them out with the many customizations that are available in the game. But the melee, that is the beauty, It is almost full interactable (ie limb targetting and dismemberment), incredibly responsive (the best FEEL i have ever gotten from a melee combat system in an open world game in which the animations, damage, and impact, looks and handles like it "should"), and a wide variety of weapons with actually impactful differences promoting a diverse set of gameplay differences between each player and each playthrough.
Dead Island's main questline is... rather dull, although it is practical for the situation at hand for the characters it is not particularly interesting and exciting. This is made up for through intresting and dark character side quests that can be found all over the environments as well as an indepth and thought provoking lore that underlines the general plot line. Still unless you explore and take advantage of the variety of sidequests to learn about the plot and characters within Dead Island you will notice that 90% of the quests you will do are fetching objects or escort missions.
In conclusion Dead Island is an open world game through and through with all the typical flaws of an openworld game. However i think the beauty of this game outweighs its flaws. Go into this game and play it like a chaotic sandbox for you to explore and enjoy. It is full of graphical issues, physics bugs, and multiple game breaking bugs.... But it is one of the greatest times you will have in a zombie game, a openworld game, and a game where you can occasionally die from opening a door.
Enjoy

If I could describe this game in one word it would be Cool. Not amazing, not brilliant, not engaging, just sheer coolness. It's extremely detailed and will amaze you when you first play it. After you test your limits and get blown up a few times, you begin to farm for money and that is when the game becomes slightly work-driven. The game can be exciting at times (as the more risky places to farm are always more profitable) but the level of fun will be dictated by the amount you are willing to risk for it.
This is what I call a "google game". Knowlege is power and the more time you spend online doing research, the more freedoms you have with this game. Learning how to explore the vastness of space will require you to study both outside and inside the game (books are needed to level up).
Also, I'm probably going to get a lot of flame for this but if you are expecting combat such as what is shown on the preview trailers, these type of things happen rarely (about once a month) and you need to be in the right type of guild for it.

As an avid Portal fan, I loved hearing about this game coming out. When someone gave it to me I immediately started playing and finished it within a couple of days. Not that I'm complaining about its shortness- I'd pretty much expected that part. However, there were some glaring errors I couldn't ignore.
The concept was pretty sound, and the use of gels to complete tasks forced me to deviate from thinking with portals, which was hard at first. However, there were parts in which I barely squeaked by because the margin for error was so small, or required extremely exact placements that weren't intuitive in the game. During the action sequence somewhere around the middle of the game, I had to navigate an obstacle course on a time limit before the area blew up. Once I got the hang of it the area was fun, but I kept dying repeatedly because of the incredibly exact gel placements and timing it required. The course was long and arduous, requiring roughly 200 restarts until I was going along smoothly and almost making it to the end. I didn't mind being challenged by the game, but it kept feeling as if they hadn't adequately checked most of these puzzles to make sure they were playable. For instance, there was absolutely no room for error on the speed run. The time limit was such that even if you completed all of the jumps and slides well you'd die from running out of time first. Even a few seconds on the clock would have helped make it slightly more playable. It didn't have the smoothness of Portal 2, and harked back to some of the original Portal's problems with precise timing which had almost been eliminated with the latter game.
Surfer dude core (I believe his name was Nigel?) was alright, though not the best option for a guide. He seemed to be a cross between Wheatley and an Aperture scientist in that he was slightly bumbling yet spouting trite guidances for the player with a distinctly Aperture flair. I couldn't really get an edge on what kind of core he was, and he didn't have a theme like the rest of the cores in the original games had. In addition, hearing him telling me to hurry up or I'd die each time I'd have to restart the obstacle course became so irritating by the end I wanted to rip his handlebars off. I won't even speak about the ending here.
All in all? It was pretty fun. Mostly. The concept was good, at least. If you don't count the fact it needed to be tested thoroughly and cleaned up before releasing. That makes sense for an mod like this, but it's still disappointing. I can forgive the core, but I can't forgive sloppy testing. For science.

Aperture Tag is a mod for Portal 2 where you cannot shoot any portals. Instead, you shoot the blue and orange gels. This was obviously inspired by Tag: The Power of Paint, the team of that game was absorbed into Valve to work on Portal 2.
Aperture Tag recycles a few levels from Portal 2, of which some are recycled from Portal 1, but with the twist in gameplay mechanics they constitute a challenge. The new levels are equally as challenging with some rather creative ideas. The mod requires a lot of mind bending, but is never unfair. Avoid spoilers, story spoilers as well as level solution spoilers.
On the negative side, some levels, especially the early ones, could use more checkpoints. But you can easily work around this by saving often.
Aperture Tag is definitely worth 5€. I had a few hours of fun with the mod, and I have not even touched the levels from the Steam Workshop yet.

Yes, I did just write two mega reviews and flood your activity feed. Anyway;
Star Wars Galactic Battlegrounds should be called Age of Empires 2: Lasers Edition (and as they’re both a pain to type I’ll call them SWGB and AOE2).
It uses the same engine as AOE2 (or AOE1 for that matter…). Same “four tiers.” Same “all civs have generic and usually useless team bonus.” Some of the upgrades are identical (farms +75 food) for the
(75 carbon/wood, 75 food). And the Market functionality is completely identical. As for the gameplay, build villagers/workers at your Town/Command Center, chop trees, harvest berry bushes, mine stone/ore, build a Castle/Fortress, train a notoriously OP Trebuchet/Cannon (yes, they’re identical), and beat the identically bad vanilla AI.
That’s not to say this is a bad game. Far from it. It's absolutely great. Coming from AOE2 I knew how the game worked and could jump straight in, and get terribly confused because an AOE2 Castle is 650 Stone and a SWGB Fortress is 550 ore. :P (Or should I say xdddddd?) If you enjoy the fun of an RTS and trying to micro absolutely everything at once then this is AOE2: Lasers Edition. And cheap, too.
Unfortunately SWGB doesn’t quite have the balance of AOE2. SWGB can be accurately summarised as “Mech Destroyers > Everything,” including more Mech Destroyers. Oh sure, there are Strike Mechs which beat troopers which beat Mounted Troopers which beat artillery which beat strike mechs… which are
beaten by Mech Destroyers. (Okay, Mounted Troopers perform
against Mech Destroyers, except that Mounted Troopers perform badly against lots of other things; troopers, air, heavy defences, when Mech Destroyers don’t).
One diversion from standard AOE2 is the introduction of aerial units – fighters, bombers, transports, and the notorious “Air Cruiser.” Except that if you bring along four Heavy AA Mobiles then you need never bother about air assaults again, and that an AA Turret can outshoot Air Cruisers. Unless you’re in
(a nice addition to a sci-fi RTS) then spaceships are entirely optional. Still very good because the AI doesn’t have a clue when to train anti-air units (it’ll send AA troopers to attack your base when you have no air despite the fact AA troopers can’t even attack ground units… gg AI)
There’s also shielding, which is pretty cool. If a unit is shielded by a generator / has self-shielding, then it regenerates a – surprise surprise – shield equal to its max HP, so a 40 HP Worker gets 40 HP worth of shielding. The Gungan unique unit is a mobile shield generator which is fantastically OP. In fact, the Gungans are OP anyway. Elite troopers (not that you need those), elite mechs (you
those), elite siege (500 dmg per hit to walls), the best UU in the entire game, a brilliant economy, and for some reason pretty good aircraft (no, I don’t get how birds beat Tie Fighters either).
Oh, and there’s also stealth. It is pretty crummy; only a couple of units (Gungan ships / upgraded Jedi) have stealth, but the counters to those (more ships than they do / Bounty Hunters) have stealth detection, so stealth is barely worth using.
There's one more difference between SWGB and AOE2, and that's the campaigns. AOE2's campaigns were
. I can't downrate them enough. About three "good" ones out of thirty-something. They were all "Here fight 5+ AI all at once and you're in the worst position possible!" Barely any variety. "Oh, and don't lose this 1HP hero or you fail the mission."
Meanwhile SWGB's campaigns are great. An absolute blast to play. Even the tutorial is fun. I... I can't reccommend the campaigns enough, they're gobsmackingly amazing for such a simplistic RTS. It's usually very difficult to make anything that isn't either a) build-and-destroy or b) an RPG with two units; but SWGB has pulled it off. Good job devs!
There is one major mod for SWGB – Expanding Fronts – which does add one new civ and some nice stuff like widescreen support (always nice). Not much else though and nothing in terms of balance (i.e. Mech Destroyers still > everything). It’s mostly a scenario editor addon with all sorts of buildings and
, except that I haven’t watched more than a quarter of Star Wars and hence go “what’s this? What’s that? What’s this spaceship? What is this supposed to be?”
There are separate AI mods that I’m installing and with a bit of luck will be more competent than the original AI (which on a 150 pop map only reaches about 70 pop…. *sigh*).

"Sang-Froid - Tales of Werevolves" is a cute, atmospheric indie tower-defense game set in 19th century Canada, involving a stand against occult forces unleashed upon a family of two brothers and a sister. It has a nice visual style, interesting (yet simple) story and quite the content for the buck. With a solid arsenal of unlockable traps and weapons, as well as skills to build, the game offers a pleasant and intellectually stimulating experience.
With various possible approaches to the missions (chapters) the game has a bit of something both for players who prefer fighting and those who prefer tactics. Yet, it seems that Sang-Froid is not as rewarding for players who carefully plan out their defenses as it should be, because with careful placement of traps and minimum involvement in combat, I was constantly out of money and struggled to get the best equipment in the first half of the game. Only after few chapters, did I discover that I could just  buy potions and kill enemies, thus saving money for the equipment. And that's a shame, because I would rather be rewarded for playing smart instead of casual. This aspect of the game is also illustrated by the fact that the character gains experience both for succeeding and failing the missions, which allows to unlock new skills either way, thus becoming stronger. It means that you can just grind through stat boosts, save money for better weapons and almost forget about trap placement in the first part of the game.
There are also some minor faults:
- Combat: the character can only move in four directions – no diagonal moves and change of a direction is not seamless; the camera movement during the fights is also a problem.
- Navigation: that mini map sure makes your head spin and you can easily go the wrong way, which could be a crucial mistake when the time is running out
- Trap placement: there is a hidden grid, but there are areas where it is not always possible to place fire wall tiles in straight lines. The game likes to add an extra tile to your desired construction sometimes, thus wasting your limited action points. It sure would have been more convenient, if it was possible to add a tile by tile and remove them tile by tile instead of all the firewall.
- Economy: the action point cost and prices for some traps doesn't seem balanced for me against their potential usefullness. For example, I never used an explosive barrel during the game, because it is an expensive trap with limited usefullness and there is a high risk of failure.
But despite its flaws "Sang-Froid" is a very good game and I recommend it to all tower-defence fans or someone who just wants to take a break from shooters like I did.
My overall rating: 8/10.

I love SLW. It's so bad. And I mean… bad. This thing is bad. Why did they need to add a specific button to run faster? What's wrong with spindash/boost on X button? Was it really necessary to add a second jump button, just to not use the homing attack? And why don't you have separate buttons for bounce and kick? I don't know. It's just another experiment by SEGA. The control itself is not too bad, there are much worse examples. But there is another problem – parkour. The game itself tells you to hold the sprint button to climb a wall and press the jump button to jump between walls, nothing else. It works fine in Desert Ruins but it doesn't in next ones. Look at Lava Mountain 3. There are some tight places with walls close to each other, like Desert Ruins. But instead of performing the wall jump, Sonic does a regular spin jump and falls to his death and another “Try again” screen. The game will never tell you that you need to hold the analog stick in the direction of an opposite wall to make it 100% work. I've never seen so complicated wall jump mechanics. They also changed the homing attack mechanic. It's now accumulating, and you can do a more powerful attack if you fully aimed at an enemy. It's pointless against regular enemies and makes easy boss fights easy as f**k. There's also no light dash for some reason, unless you use a certain wisp on the one and only stage. Yeah, there are wisps in this game. And they are pointless. In Sonic Colors, they were a part of the plot and stages were designed to use different color powers. But not in this game. There are some places where you need to use wisps but in most cases you can easily skip them. Some wisps came from Colors, the new ones are weird and unnecessary. Especially, the one that transforms you into a note.
The level design is freaky. Most of stages are tubes or spheres floating in the air. 2D sections are rounded, gravity constantly changes direction. Sonic feels extremely slow in 2D, even if I spindash for some seconds. Badniks as common enemies. Again. But now they are gigantic (yeah, that mad scientist with IQ of 300 couldn't think up something better, after so many games). The introduced kick attack is useful against most of them but not against bosses. It can only break the defense of a certain boss but it doesn't deal any damage, that's odd. Some gimmicks are just… WTF? We play another food-themed stage, we travel in jets of juice, we run from homing fruits, we transform into a snowball, we jump on flowers, some of them even work as cannons, we play a kind of a inverted version of Flappy Bird, etc. “Welcome to Sonic Team. We make games, I think.” This game is full of borrowing. Basically, it feels like Super Mario Galaxy with Sonic. Besides, this game uses a lot of common features from classic platformers. It's not bad, it's just cheap.
The plot is forgettable. It doesn't even try to explain things. The Deadly 6 are actually the Cliche 6. I don't even remember their names, after 10+ hours. Graphics are nice but the style of the game sucks. I've heard about performance problems but I've never encountered them on my 5 years old PC. The game seems to be better optimized than Sonic Generations but I suppose it's because Generations is a lot more detailed. The soundtrack is also poor, but better than in later released Sonic Boom. No main vocal theme (like Generations), most of tracks don't fit the stages but tbh even Crush 40's music wouldn't fit stages like these. The stages also don't match their names. There is no wind in Windy Hill, no ruins in Desert Ruins, floating in the air Tropical Coast doesn't look like a coast, casino is not frozen, Silent Forest 3 is actually ice level without even a glimpse of a forest, Sky Road… okay, it's in the sky (like other stages), Lava Mountain has lava and water-themed act 2. There's also the Hidden World, the most bizarre stages in the game. Featuring furry Pacman. Bosses, like I said before, are extremely easy. Most of them are defeated in 2 fully aimed homing attacks, in some cases even 1 hit is enough. The final boss is an inferior copy of Nega-Wisp Armor. Boring.
The achievements aka Omochao missions are easy but tedious. The biggest problem is that they don't count your previous progress (so you'll replay a lot of stages to grind rings/enemies/etc.) and you can only take 3 missions at once. Clearing all missions takes about the same time as 100% completing Sonic Generations but it's a lot more boring.

It's just mediocre, I've cleared the game with poker face and some WTF-ing. If you're looking for a good Sonic game, play Freedom Planet. I'm glad that I got this game as a gift. I'd never actually buy a game like this. Sonic (has) lost (his) world. :(

When it comes to games, I tend to be quite interested in Early Access games, as they have the ability to improve and change the way they play, depending on the feedback given. With Celestial Breach, I was unsure what to think in the beginning. An arcade style flying game? Sounded fun so I bought it the week it came out and booted it up.
The game surprised me quite a bit, as I wasn't expecting the exceedingly beautiful graphics, nor was I expecting the promt updates that the developers were pushing out. Let's start with how my first experience with the game went.
I booted up the game to find quite a pleasant menu screen, with all the options that a game would have needed. I adjusted the graphics to push my system as far as the game could (ultra), and then proceeded to check the keybindings. The game seems to be coded on a Swiss keyboard (I don't know what other keyboards are like this), as the Y and the Z key seem to be in different locations, with Y, by default, being for the flares (I know, didn't seem intuitive). After quickly adjusting my keybindings (will have them below in the feedback section), I went to the menu and pressed start. To my surprise, there was not a single server running, but oh well, it had only just been released and this is still the first week of the games release (I believe).
I then hosted my own server, and attempted to play the game as I would any game. Fly, shoot and blow everything in sight up. I died quite promptly and was forced to restart. The graphics were stunning though. There are some areas in which the graphics could improve (will be listed below), however, the overall look of the game is astonishing.
Once I figured out how to play the game properly, I had such fun. I boosted the difficulty up and flew around the skies of the maps like a madman. I then moved to my next step. I tried to get my friends to buy the game. "5 person coop" is advertised so naturally I wanted to try it (I still haven't been able to). None of my friends were too willing to buy a game that had so few reviews, so I resorted to the steam discussions and the discord server (the devs had this up and running so soon in development!). I asked around and found a player that wanted to play some Coop. We played for a bit and had a blast, with both of us wrecking havoc left, right and center. Oh boy, that was a blast.
After forcing my friends to come and try out this new game on my computer, I managed to convince two of them to buy it. After having played a few hours with them, I asked them what they thought of the game and if they had had fun. One of them was very happy with his purchase and wished to join the discord, and the other didn't respond and simply shot me with the railgun, in denial that I had proven him wrong about a game he thought was not going to be too fun in the long run.
Now here for the pros and cons of the game, but there will be no cons, simply stuff I would change/add!
Well, that was my entire review. If you read the whole thing, thank you very much for taking your time to go through all of it :)

The game is basically a tower defence where you have about 4 buildings(later on) scattered across the map. Your objective is to protect these buildings while eliminating hostile beasts. You can reroute the beasts' paths and set traps along the way. You also have access to an axe, a rifle and a various potions and protective items. These become available for upgrade later on.
It can get hectic at times as the game is not very forgiving and you need to maximize the beasts' route into your traps given the limited resources.

Very flawed game but it grows on you if you can look past the numerous flaws. It's good enough to kill time on a lazy weekend.
It is short but fun.

I played this game when it was required to pay to do so and received a free month with the ownership pack on sale and figured I'd try it out. I didn't even tap into the corporation system to explore the cooperative nature of the game as I wanted to build my in-game capital up to the point where I had more options to expand my play.  Chiefly, I started mining asteroids to increase my capital in a lucrative way so that I could branch into the other areas of the game, but life happened and other things took priority, but now I believe that it might be more fun now, but for an experience, it's definitely worth at least a shot, and form your own opinions first by first-hand accounts.

I liked the initial release and I like the Definitive Edition even more primarily because technical issues have been resolved. Definitive Edition doesn't have some of the technical issues that the original had, but I did pull the FOV from 65 to 85.
This is why I like this game:
- EASY, the big enemies are easy to take out once you know their weaknesses, also, just keep moving
- It's fun because it's not grindy, you'll level abilities and craft weapons, but the progression is balanced
- The graphics and sound are very good
- The environment feels legitimate, the audio/visual experience really makes me feel like I'm in a tropical environment
- Somewhat cheesy acting, I love that stuff, it's not like a movie, it's like a video game!
- Only got stuck in the map/environment once, really not buggy at all
I played through Definitive Edition on an i7-6700K + GTX 1080, it ran smooth maxed out, not hitchy like the original. If you liked the original and are considering this, buy it on sale and give it another playthrough.

Superfight is a game where you have to debate why your character would win in fight to death against your enemy.
The game consists of 3 rounds (2 if you're playing game of 3 players) where 2 random pairs of players will be formed and will fight in 2 minutes of crazy debate. Winners of both rounds will then fight against eachother in a final round.
Round starts off by making you draw 3 characters and 3 attributes. You select character and attribute after which game draws you one final attribute and location and scenario where the fight takes place. After this everything is debatable. You have to do whatever it takes to convince your fellow players (and Twitch viewers if even one of you are streaming) that you are THE winner. The argument happens in real time using your microphone and webcam, there is no text chat.
While at first this might seem all confusing, maybe boring, after playing 7 hours I can tell you - It isn't. If you are person that enjoys talking and debating this is a game for you. You will run in crazy arguments all the time and unless you are a crazy master debator you WILL get the "why-the-actual-♥♥♥♥ didn't I think of that?" -feeling causing you to re-think everything because of opposing argument you simply can't find defense to.
I personally am not native american nor british for all that matters, my english isn't perfect so I tend to be shy when it comes to face-to-face conversations. So far I have a feeling that this game is helping me adjust. When the bell rings there is no escape (well, except the leave match button for all you chickens out there) so unless you want to be that guy who froze on live you have to talk and this pressure is good way to get rid of any type of stagefright
The game has one problem - playerbase at this time is annoyingly small. With new steam refund policy however you can buy game and if you don't get match in reasonable time refund it. Playerbase seems to be growing lately though so I don't think this will be a problem for long.
If you're a person (or anything else that can browse Internet, is able to speak english and has MICROPHONE - yes, the MICROPHONE IS REQUIRED) that enjoys a good argument every while and then and don't get annoyed with possible mature content (mature cards can be disabled but of course this don't prevent people from speaking R-rated stuff. Usually R-rated people though want to have mature cards enabled so problem is small. There are also no images) this is a game for you.
My personal rating for this game would be 8/10. If we would get more players and maybe somekind of tournament mode to host own tournaments it would be 9.5/10, just to leave little space for improvement.

Ahhh Eve Online... where to begin?
I've played this on and off for a few years. Mostly as part of a large corp in a large alliance. If you want to get anywhere, you need to do the same. Been in some large battles that were pretty damn fun, camped some gates for fun and profit. Got my ♥♥♥♥♥♥handed to me in a wormhole on multiple occasions. Generally killed and died a lot.
I've done a little time AFK mining (boring as hell) and some exploration and mostly PVP. When I was most into it, it was like an abusive relationship.... maybe this time it'll be better? Got podded again.
Terms like "bitter vets" applies to most of the ridiculously powerful older players, extremely resistant to change and always waxing poetic over "the good ol days".
The golden rule, which will be pounded into your head the instant you leave HiSec will be: NEVER FLY WHAT YOU CAN'T AFFORD TO LOSE.
The changes to the clones states (alpha/omega) etc seemed like a good idea to me, but haven't played it too much in recent times despite having an alpha clone sitting in dock with two Plex (worth a month full subscription each). The main reason for not playing is this: This game, to be played properly is a full time job. I'm not even kidding. It takes lots of learning (the famous learning "cliff" rather than curve) and to be honest, the whole thing is rather stagnant. It doesn't draw me in anymore. Sometimes I think to myself, "I should fire up my ships, rejoin corp and get into it again"... but then I get a feeling similar to thinking about work on monday morning. This game was amazing, beautiful, crazy and complex. But it is also, past its time now. I given it a thumbs up for the many hours I enjoyed, even if, I'm unlikely to ever play it again. To those who think this game is pay to win, it's not. You gotta learn how to make isk properly. High-sec wont cut it, for starters.
It's not meant to be easy for an alpha to make isk, I would consider being an alpha as a way to support big corporations and a way to slooowly inch your way toward a PLEX. Once you reach your first PLEX, you'll get a lot of congratulatory salutes from your corp-mates for one, but you'll also be able to skill train much faster and ultimately get more income. The first push is the hardest, then it gets so much easier as time progresses.
Most people, however, still recommend that you go straight into buying a PLEX or having a friend support you with one. It will get you into the 'real' game faster and you'll feel a lot more satisfied.
Every one of you should consider joining a nullsec corp and giving ratting a try for 6-10 mil ticks. There are plenty of corps out there that accept alphas / completely fresh players. Eventually once you reach a PLEX, you can upgrade your ratting ship and get even better ticks, 12 to 17 mil, and at that point- you can do havens which can give you a chance of a shadow serpentis ship (which can drop up to 100 million isk, and, very rarely, 1 billion), and an escalation which can range in price from 80 million to 150 million. Remember that a PLEX is worth around 1.3 billion in todays market.
Add multiboxing to this method and you can double, triple, quadruple.. whatever -uple you can think of -- your profit. It requires a lot of setting up though. I have at least 500 hours outside of steam and I still only got 2 accounts that run ratting sites simultaneously (mind you, I was a bit lazy)
There are also a lot of corps which have ratters that give out salvages (wreckages that drop from ratting sites), which you can claim, and earn a solid 12-15 mil.. and it only takes 15 to 20 minutes.
EVE is known to be a waiting / market simulator. It's meant for a very specific audience, which CCP is trying to expand (and, admittedly, failing a bit at doing so).
One more thing. If you know any nerds or anyone who likes space battles who aren't very lazy and are willing to learn new things (this is what I mean by specific audience), try and get them into playing EVE. They won't regret it.
That's all I have to say. This game has passed the mountain and is indeed starting to fall, but very slowly at that. Remember that this game is over 12 years old. Let's hope for a better tomorrow. 07

When I first looked at all the bad review of this game, I had seconds thoughts. But as a Portal fan, I had to at least try it out. It was worth it. Everybody is complaining how the game is short, but remember, this is a mod, not a full game. It is bound to be short and have a few bugs here and there. I really enjoyed it.
Scoring:
- People complain about redone levels. There were only 2 or 3 of them. The others were pretty challenging in some spots. Especially the "Nature" looking levels.
- Although it is a new mechanic, there isn't much you could do with the Paint Gun. But the developers did as much as they could with it. They couldv'e made it a little better looking though.
- Yes, Nigel was a bit of a flat character, but he still has heart. There is alot worse voice acting out there. Don't forget, this is a mod, not a full game. So it won't have top notch professional voice actors. (No offense to the guy voicing Nigel)
- 9/10 - The ending confused me a bit. But when I nocliped and looked around the ending room, I found something interesting. (Not going to spoil it completely) There is another ending, so go look for it!
- 9/10 - This game has much potential and is worth the money for a short "expansion" of a game francise that I love. Can't wait to see what comes next.

This game does suffer a bit from Telltale's "lack of actual consequences from choices", although it does have a lot more than others.
It is however, by far, the best Telltale game of this genre that they've made. Don't listen to the stooges who say that it's TWD. They're wrong. This game has more to it than the three TWD games put together. The plot is strong, the characters are all memorable, and you actually feel for them. The game is 200% hilarious, and the scenes are brilliantly done to keep up a tone of light heartedness throughout most of the game. The moments when emotions change for various, well thought out reasons actually affect you emotionally. I admit that the game did nearly bring me to tears on one occasion, and was almost as successful twice more. It will make you angry, it will make you incredibly satisfied, and it will make you smile and laugh far more frequently than any other game.
Buy it. Play it. I hadn't played Borderlands at all before this game. Loved every minute of it.

Do you like to actively complain as you play a game? Sonic Lost World's got you. It has controls as frustrating as its level design, its music as underwhelming as its boss fights, and best of all, this game (unlike most GOOD Sonic games) isn't over in an hour or two. Lost World is a Lost Cause.
In the famous words of Benjamin Frankin, "Those who sacrifice Sonic's Speed for Super Mario Galaxy deserve neither and lose both." Sonic's revised control scheme, which consists of a run (read: NOT 'boost', but run) button, two jump buttons that serve different uses, and a new parkour system that will get you killed almost as much as the pitfall-ridden hellhole that is most of the game's stages, isn't all too great. The only thing keeping me playing through the adventure is Mike Pollock's Eggman, the promise that the game will end at some point, and the fact that I paid for it.
I wanted to like this game for what it was trying to do. I can forgive a bad Sonic game, but a Sonic game this clearly isn't. The music sucks outside of like, two levels, and everything else sucks aside from like, two levels. The graphics are nice, but for some reason all the enemy designs are direct copies of enemies from better Sonic games. I want to say it was an artistic decision, but deep down I know this is the case because they just recycled assets from Sonic Generations.
Speaking of Sonic Generations, that game is legit. Play that instead. There's a modding community there, so enjoy some glorious new mod levels. This one was for charity, I hope my sacrifice was not in vain.

TL:DR - Only recommend on sale, with caution.
Got this game from the Humble Bundle of Sonic's 25th just to play this game, and I was a little disappointed. It's decent, but has a lot of issues. Here's what I mean.
The Good
+The items. It was nice to see Sonic's items come back, such as the shields, invincibility, etc. Though you have to do missions or randomly get them from the world map, They're a nice addition, and being able to hold up to 5 to use at any time can be useful.
+Super Sonic. Whereas he was a bit disappointing in recent games, unlocking him in this game feels pretty well-earned. Plus as long as you have 50+ rings, you can switch out any time! it's a nice addition.
+The music. It roughly holds up to the status quo of recent Sonic games. It's not too bad.
The Good but Bad/Can be Better
~Sonic's moves. He got a lot better at parkouring, and he's got a lot of nice moves, like running on walls, wall jumping both horizontally and vertically, the works. While they're cool, they could've been implemented better/more consistent. Sometimes he'll run on the wall just fine, others he won't.
~The controls in general. They're a little weird to get used to, such as having to constantly hold RT to run else I'll be slow as molasses. It's not like having a Boost meter where you're somewhat fast without it. Some things aren't even explained, such as being able to spindash for a very long time. You may die a fair amount, but later in the game you get extra lives handed to you like candy, so it's tolerable.
~The levels. I like most of the zones and some of the level themes! The first level led me to believe that you'd be able to complete levels in multiple different ways with each level since the first one had branching paths. That held true for a select few levels. The others felt rather linear. Not bad, but mislead me personally. Also, a lot of people compare this to Mario Galaxy, and for the most part, it's more inspired by.
~The wisps. I liked seeing them again, and there's a lot of them! Some old, some new. However, a lot of them are underutilized and/or annoying to use. Aiming the rocket in 3D can be harder than needbe, and while the bomb is cool, I feel like it's not useful aside from clearing the few missions it's used for. Speaking of...
The Minorly Bad
=I dealt with a few glitches, but none of them are too game-breaking, such as death on an open ceiling.
The Bad
-Mission mode. It's so horrible and tedious, and most of my playtime was just plowing through them. It's not like most games where you have progressive milestones and can just continue working consistently. "Collect 100/250/500/1000/whatever (up to 4500) rings" has to be randomly picked from Omochao, and you can only get up to 3 missions at a time. Some of them are really tedious and don't need to be, and some are flatout near impossible! (Wall jump 20 times in a row, how many places can you do that? Oh wait you can slide down a little to get more movement). So if anyone wants to get achievements, good luck. Also, you don't unlock anything from doing them all.
-Final boss. Feels like a watered down version from
Not a satisfying ending.
-Price. Definitely not worth $30. I got mine from $10 thanks to Humble Bundle, and I don't recommend paying more than that.
Overall, it's not too bad to kill some time, but it does get frustrating and has assets that aren't utilized to their fullest potential.

DRAGON BALL XENOVERSE is an action RPG, fighting game from DIMPS and BANDAI NAMCO Entertainment. Let’s get rocking.
The Good
I went into this game knowing two things about Dragon Ball. One, when I was younger, my older brother had a friend that watched the show. Two, I have a friend that watched the show when he was younger. Well, I knew those two things and one more thing: Dragon Ball is pretty much synonymous with overly dramatic screaming. While none of this is really information you can form an opinion with, at some point in my life, I imagined Dragon Ball wasn’t really something that would float my boat. Enter DRAGON BALL XENOVERSE and holy♥♥♥♥♥♥was I wrong.
I’m not good at traditional fighting games. I typically end up getting my♥♥♥♥♥handed to me repeatedly on platters made of varying precious metals. Knowing that Dragon Ball is practically constant fighting, made me additionally skeptic that this game would be something I’d like. Now, if you’ve ever had the pleasure of playing Phantom Dust on the original Xbox, think about how that plays. Now combine that with a watered down and far less graphic of Mortal Kombat. You know have a pretty good idea of how DRAGON BALL XENOVERSE plays.
No matter what your play style is, you can easily build a character to complement it. You want to be speedy as all hell and punch people a thousand times? DBX has you covered. You want to sit back and shoot gigantic laser beams out of your mouth, eyes, and other orifices? DBX has you covered. This game has something for every play style.
Character customization is simple, but it was just right. You can be one of five races (three of which feature gender selection) and you can build your character towards being up close and personal, a master of Ki attacks, or a balance between the two.
This game has a great many missions to it. The main story I didn’t really understand as well as I could have (I assume it makes more sense if you’ve seen the show), but the missions are fun nonetheless. You’ve got the stuff you do for the main quest and the stuff you do on the side. They’re all pretty short, but they feel like they’re just the right length. There’s only so long you can mash buttons before your fingers begin to wear out anyway.
I can’t really explain why, but I just kept coming back to this game for more. I have several different characters above level 50 and each one is a different build. Once you get the hang of it, you’ll be itching to try new things and new styles of play.
The Bad
I don’t really have anything bad to say about this one.
The Meh
Going into this game blind (blind here having the meaning of not knowing who anyone was or what the hell was going on) was a tiny bit stressful, but names and faces become familiar quick. If you know your vegetables and musical instruments, you pretty much know 1/3 of the characters’ names.

I bought this game on sale today, on the Humble Bundle website. I thought, hey, might as well give it a try. It's cheap, sorta bored, indie game, not very large file, etc. So I bought it, and downloaded it, and started it up.
Wasn't exactly sure what I was getting into, but it was love at first site. The game is humorous, and acknowledges many different playstyles of people. Run & Gun, Stealth, "do it for the story," and yes, even "I'm just here to have a good time and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥up." The game accomodates all of those. The Achievements don't feel tedious, and reward silly little things as well.
I'm writing this just as I finished the story. I'm a player that does each separate mission, in many different ways. I might go Run & Gun on some, and Stealth on others, but I do enjoy a good story. And this game's story was quite good. Not sure how the replayability is, considering the story is sort of linear, but it does have some branching elements. This game definitely had me captivated for the two hours I played it. Don't let my short play time fool you, the game is still a lot of fun, and definitely worth the buy. I seriously enjoyed every minute of it. Some levels are challenging, some are very easy. Each one has its own little puzzles that you the player will have to figure out how to solve to complete the level, but it is still very fun.
Design: 10/10
The artwork and design of the game is fairly top notch. Pixel-graphics are becoming popular again, but this game does it right. Never are you thinking that they are trying too hard.
Sound/Music: 8/10
I loved the soundtrack. Even though it got a bit repetitive, but lets be honest, what game's soundtrack doesn't? Each sound in game, was very well designed. Doors opening, gunshots, windows breaking, etc. It was all very crisp. Rated it an 8/10 for the repetiveness, but don't let that put you off.
Gameplay Mechanics: 9/10
Very fluid motions. It's a two dimensional platformer, so there isn't much to go into this, but it still felt very fluid. There were only minor bugs, and even then, nothing that was even remotely gamebreaking.
Story: 9/10
I give this a 9/10 only because it felt too short. But all in all, great story. The game just felt a bit short, even though throughout its entirety, I was having fun.
Overall: 9/10
Definitely a great purchase. I enjoyed every moment of it. I would definitely recommend this game to most anyone I know, especially those who feel adventurous, and feel like giving a sort-of different game a chance.

A lot of technical issues from the original version of this game like the damaged draw distance and mouse/keyboard controls have been fixed. It is now much more playable and enjoyable. Unfortunatelly these technical improvements are just not enough for Dead Island to overcome it's still mediocre story, terrible characters, a very weak/uneven voice acting and in my opinion it's biggest weakness which would be repetitiveness. The body destruction system in this game brings a lot of fun but after decapitating countless numbers of zombies I just ran out of steam (no pun intended) and the very boring and similar/blunt side quests didn't help at all. Also the need to animate a lot of the attacks our playable character performes sometimes felt like it took away control from me/the player, but it's not on the same level of bad as e.g the Thief reboot game. It's quite passable. Basically the game just felt very blunt, like it was only made for money and the developers didn't have any passion/fun producing it. Techland(the company which made this game) is known for being a kind of a mixed bag when it comes to making games. Sometimes they make terrific titles like Call of Juarez, and other times garbage which this game is a perfect example of. I would treat Dead Island or Dead Island Definitive Edition as kind of a testing ground for Techland's much better title - Dying Light. This game is just awesome. It might be the company's best one so far. In conclusion, don't buy Dead Island Definitive Edition on steam. It will only discourage you from buying Techalnd's games which are actually great. Go straight to Dying Light. It has fluid, entertaining controls and some of the side quests are terrific. The voice acting, while not perfect is significantly better and the game can actually sometimes build up tension.

I'm not sure why people say it is bad that you have to pay $7.00 for this game. I mean, it was made with a lot of effort. I think it deserves to be payed for. Anyway, all I am saying is, you really SHOULD get it.
In the aftermath of Portal 2 Co-Op, GLaDOS has a lot of subjects to choose from. After designing their final product, Aperture Science's Handhelp Paint Gun, you wake up, playing as a random subject. A core, named Nigel, guides you through 16 chambers to test this new product.

I'm really starting to dig noir stuff now. Why? Because of Gunpoint.
Gunpoint is a 2d sidescrolling stealth game that let's you play as a freelance spy who'll accept any contract as long as he get's his payday, and you can approach each mission however you want. Want to be a pacifist? you can do it, you want to do it like a Ninja? You can do it, or do you want to be an absolute psychopath and shoot or punch your way through everyone? Well you're in luck, you can do that too.
Story: You play as Richard Conway, who one night falls into a window from another building. A murder ensues and you get involved into corporate espionage between two corporations, Rooke and Intex. From this point on you have control of how the game's narrative goes, due to the multiple dialogue choices you can choose from each conversation with each character that hire's Richard. In this sense, Richard can either be a complete♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ a smart person who covers his tracks, a funny but sometimes awkward person you get the idea. The dialouge is really funny and the characters themselves are pretty good and are affected by your decisions. It's actually fun to mess around with these characters and play both sides. All in all it's a choice and consequence game and it's a fun ride that warrants a few playthroughs just to say what results you get.
Gameplay: Gunpoint uses 2d sidescrolling that is mainly focused on utilising stealth. It's challenging because it's very easy to get killed, not to mention that you'll encounter alarms, security cameras, motion detecters and locked doors. Planning on how you'll get in, aquiring the item/data and getting out sucessfully is what you'll be doing each mission, the only difference is the security layout, building size and how many guards are there. You can upgrade how high you jump and how quick you can do it, also you can buy a variety of equipment that makes things easier, like a crosslink for instance.
The Crosslink device that you get early in game, let's you connect security systems into other security systems that enables you to cleverly get around the building. For example, I crosslink a lightswitch to a door, I turn on/off the switch, I can open the door. what's great about this game is not just the choice you have in the narrative, but it's also the choice of how you want to approach missions.
Graphics and Music: I used to dislike retro-inspired graphics, but my viewpoint towards it has been toning down ever since then. I appreciate it more than ever now, and in Gunpoints case, I'm glad the developers went with this direction, because Gunpoint just stands out and has a really cool theme to back it up. Speaking of music, It's Jazz that soothes into your ears, making you feel like you're in a noir-film or a spy movie, it's badass.
Overall: The only disappointing thing I can come up with is that it's too short and I wish it was longer. I was thinking that you could freely take any contract and have mutiple storylines going on. Regardless, Gunpoint is now part of Steam workshop and there are plenty of custom made maps to choose from. For only $10.00 it's a really enjoyable game that has replay value, awesome music, awesome gameplay, funny dialogue and characters.

[HOW TO PLAY]
SUPERFIGHT is essentially a game where you debate and/or roleplay to see who comes out as the winner. To figure out who becomes the winner, both players receive three cards each. One white card being the person/entity, and two black cards which are the attributes applied to the white card. However, there are two cards at the bottom of the screen. The one on the left being where the fight is located (blue card), and the one on the right which is the event that effects both players (purple card). Whoever makes a better argument as to why they deserve winning rights is biased between the two other spectators in the match and people voting via Twitch if you're livestreaming. This is a game where pros and cons are critically applied. Whatever combination of cards you receive, that can either help you or hurt you. With that being, let's move on.
[PROS]
- Lots of cards to choose from to keep the game interesting.
- Twitch integration so viewers can vote.
- Great music.
- Nice sound effects.
[CONS]
None, really.
[PERSONAL REVIEW]
In my opinion, this game is all about replay value. You could play SUPERFIGHT for hours on end. This is probably one of my favorite games on Steam.

A point & click game with a wacky story, difficult puzzles, and many funny moments.
Some of the humor can go right over your head, but a majority of it will catch on. It’s a hit or miss depending on what kind of humor you enjoy. There are numerous references from many different sources, so good luck finding and identifying all of them!
The story follows a young man named Otto Thompson. Unfortunately for Otto, after responding to an appealing date, he is kidnapped and transported to an old underground Russian bunker. You must escape captivity, find a way out of the stony prison, and find out who is behind all of this.
You can expect a normal playthrough to take 3-4 hours, or less if you use a walkthrough. The gameplay is highly focused on puzzles, as most other point & clicks are.
The puzzles focus on sharp observation of environment and lots of trial and error. The puzzles can feel tedious after a while and I had to consult a guide a fair amount of times when the objective was not clear. Then again, I’m not the best when it comes to environmental queues or solving puzzles. It is nice to note that not all the puzzles are alike: they vary in length and difficulty. Additionally, the main character gives hints if you inspect certain items.
Another feature to this game is the 33 hidden achievements, which can be unlocked in numerous ways. My favorite is secret # 4: KONA-code, where you input part of the Konami code on the save/load screen using the arrow keys located on the same page. Up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right. If you like secrets, you should try and unlock all 33 of these conspicuous achievements.
I would also like to add that there is a mini game that you can play towards the end called Swords & Fireballs VII. It’s short, but fun (~15 min).
The bad parts of this game are the price and amount of content. For a $10 game, 3-4 hours of content isn’t that much. Unless you have no problem spending money, I would advise that you think twice before buying, or just wait for a sale to purchase this title. I did not run into any glitches, unless you call the game starting up in German a glitch. I simply fixed this by going into the settings and changing the language to English.
Overall, this is a point & click game with a humorous story that doesn’t bring much new to the table gameplay wise. If you like point & clicks, definitely put this on your list to check out. Looking back, I am greatly reminded of another point & click adventure game I played a few months back, MechaNika (but MechaNika has a more affordable price tag of $4).

First, this game is for Naruto fans only.  Do not buy if you don't get a rock hard boner from hearing anything about Naruto.
Now my review.  Wow.  This game is hot garbage.  The one on one battles aren't too bad at times.  A bit repetitious but you get used to the mechanics eventually.  The story is a bit boring as you just run the gauntlet of point A to point B (when the game allows it) then a battle.  99% of the game(?) has turned into me pressing start and skipping.  I really wanted to finish the game but once I got to the end, it's just a huge clusterf***.  What should have been a good idea was quickly filled with rage quit inducing moment.  Breaking the rules of the game so the antagonists get special treatment and powerups is fine if it calls for it, but when you're fighting multiple enemies and your in game camera starts shooting all over the place like Michael J. Fox shooting the Blair Witch combined with Cloverfield and you have no clue where you're at.  The in-battle cutscenes are super-f***ing annoying, where I skipped almost every other cutscene in the game, this makes me sit through 10 minutes of still framed shots with voice over.  Not too mention some a$$hat's bright idea it was to keep your health down when you progress in the story.  Immersive, right?  No, because the only way to reheal it is too go to the one ramen restaurant in the game to heal.  You can't access the health packs in your inventory, no that's stupid.  Not too mention in the final fights when you're fighting 10 story tall monsters, which should be the fun climactic battle of the game, sh*ts it's pants like a 4 year old eating Mexican food.  The developers hid fine little details on how to fight in the battles, which is interesting and can prove to be a fun mechanic, but quickly turns into that time your uncle wanted to play "wrestling".  Plus the item system is basically throwing a single tomato into a salad.  Yeah, it's there but it feels like it doesn't belong and there should be more with it.  I'm thinking way too much into this. Your time would be better spent to just go on youtube and watch someone else play it cause this is not worth the time.  I guess I'll just uninstall it and let it gather electronic dust in my Steam library.

So back when this game was initially released on the Wii U I didn't pick it up because of all of the negative reviews I heard.  However I recently picked up the game via Humble Bundle.  Sonic Lost World is a very mixed experience, but I think the Pros out weigh the Cons.  First, while I didn't like the concept of the spherical level design at first (I would've preferred a level design mentality closer to Generations or Colors) I found it to be mostly fine.  The cylindrical/spherical design rarely gave me any issues.  The graphics also look very nice, on par with if not better than Sonic Generations.  I did have some some slow down issues at first, but bumping the resolution down from 1080p to 720p fixed that and the game almost always ran at 60fps (the water levels gave my computer a bit of a hard time and the gameplay slowed down a lot, but not to an unplayable point).  The story also, while not the best the series has to offer, at least allows for some interesting interactions between Sonic, Tails, and Eggman.  I have to say though, my biggest issue with this game has to be controller support.  While the game does have it, it even says that it is better experienced with a controller before you even make it to the main menu, the support isn't the best.  I use a normal first party Xbox 360 USB controller to play games on my PC and sometimes upon launching the game my controller would just not even work with this game.  Restarting Steam or my computer normally fixed it, but it can be a pain in the butt when you want to just play a game and have to jump through a few hoops to get it to work.  However, I think the fun gameplay of this game outweighs the negatives.  I don't think it is the best game in the series, but if you are dying for some more Sonic like I was then this game is worth it!

Sang Froid is a wonderful Indie game.
To quickly sum up this game, it's an action-based tower defense with a story tacked on to boot.  You set up your traps during the day and defend your buildings at night using traps, axe, and rifle.
The monsters come in waves and you need to set up your traps and your positioning to respond to the monsters and their path (which you can later manipulate).
Combine that with a levelling system (arguably on rails as if you survive the night, you'll level but even in failure, you can level up) in which I have yet to find a single ability which wouldn't be useful depending on playstyle. There are two playable characters which determine the difficulty of the game. Jos is a tough strong guy whereas his brother Jack is better with a gun but not as tough.
I had a really good time with this game however, there was not a great deal of play time available. You need to survive 20 nights and the story completes itself. There are plans for a Sang Froid 2 however, the company just released Conflicks on Steam and the follow up might be a while in the making.  I would also have loved perhaps some more choice in the story but for their first effort, Sang Froid was a gem.
I would give it a 8.5 out of 10 but totally worth your time and money.

This game took up a lot of hours of days last week. I really enjoyed it. To put it bluntly, this is not a great game by any means. I wouldn't even go as far as to say it was good. But it was fun. It was so fun I'd be playing with my mouth open saying, "wooooaaaah" like I did watching the Anime when I was 10. It's such a broad term but this game is cool. It's cool and it's fun.
My favorite part of this game is being able to play as your own custom character. It was so awesome being there with my favorite characters as we relived the challenges Goku and friends faced throughout the show. The move system is so well integrated and worked smoothly. Character customization in the beginning lacked a little bit but overall it was solid.
My biggest problem with this game is the lack of substance in the enviorment. The hub world is boring and bland, NPC's without any heavy voice acting made everything feel empty. The cutscenes were enjoyable but felt awkward when the game tried to make it seem like my character had any relation to the other characters. This game could have really benefited from a voiced protagonist or at least dialogue options. I felt like I was on a linear path the whole time and my character's feelings really didn't matter. The lack of choice in the story made me feel like a puppet rather than a hero. Towards the end, the game is really pushing a buddy system with Trunks. Which would be fine if my character had any sort of personality. But he didn't, so every push at friendship and connection felt forced and awkward.
However, the game makes up for it's lack of enviormental substance with the combat. The fighting wasn't the most complex but as I'm pretty bad at fighting games I accpeted this with open arms. Combat is insane and chaotic. It feels amazing and it's extremely smooth. The way the custom skill sets work allow the player to make their own combos and play styles very easily. There is so much depth in the combat but yet it's so simple. It's fun, it's cool, and I enjoyed it and really that's what really matters in games. It was well worth the $12 I paid for it during the Steam Summer Sale however I wouldn't recommend buying it full price. It'll keep you entertained for at least 3 days to a week which is well worth a sale price.

The game succeeds in allowing you to play Othello on Steam utilizing different match parameters including local/online coop and solo play with various difficulty levels. Although I enjoyed playing this game, the UI and graphics along with minimal personalization options leave a desire for more. If you like Othello at all or want to add another (strategy) board game to your collection, I definitely recommend getting this game.
Othello is a classic board game, and this Steam game with the same name manages to bring back the old school nostalgia without hampering the gameplay. For those that have never played Othello before, your objective is to have the majority of stones "flipped" when there are no moves available. Your opponent's stones are flipped when you place an adjacent stone, assuming that a line is created in which your opponent's stones are bounded by yours.
In this game you have the ability to: play against AI with multiple difficulty levels, pass and play for local coop, or play online against other users. The online feature provides a game browser with custom matches including ranked play. You even have the ability to utilize asynchronous play - you can quit the game and receive a notification when it's your turn. The online community seems to be hanging on by a thread, though it's possible I looked at the browser list at unpopular times.
Regarding solo play, the AI is fairly difficult on Hard and above difficulty levels (Beginner < Easy < Medium < Hard < Harder < Hardest). As a casual player, I get crushed almost every time playing the higher difficulties. Due to this, I really would have liked an easy Restart button. There is also no save feature against the AI for those that like to play at a slower pace or come back at another time.

How about an objective review?
Yes, it plays much like a clone of Super Mario Galaxy on varying degrees, but that is far from a bad thing. Once you figure out how Sonic's moves work with the physics and the significance of color powers in certain areas, this is a great platformer based around momentum and playing off the environment around you. It is a true child of the golden age of Collect-a-thons and deserves more credit than it gets. Honestly, I think many people would have liked this game better if it starred someone other than the Sonic crew, as their name in 3d platformers has been tarnished by the likes of Shadow, Sonic 06, Unleashed, and the Wii Exclusives like Black Knight.
Bottom Line:
Closest you'll get to Super Mario Galaxy on Steam at the moment. How is that bad?

Just played about an hour of this game. Got it with a HumbleBundle and I gotta say it's really a throwback to Sonic 2. I know people like Pros and Cons lists, so here it goes:
Pros:
-Nice graphics.
-Great cutscenes
-Enemy detection and combos work great
-Plenty of variety
-Worlds are only a few levels, but make up for that with plenty of worlds (wouldn't it be biomes since this is all on the same planet? Idk.)
-Just the right amount of frustrating
-Voice acting is great
-Soundtrack is good, but could be better. (this is a pro, because the soundtrack doesn't blow. It IS good. I just feel like it could be a bit better)
Cons:
-Everything feels kinda slow. There are parts where the speed does pick up (like how you want a sonic game to be) but the majority of it you just feel like Sonic is holding back. This is a major flaw in all the 3D Sonic games. Not just this one.
-Color powerups are finicky. They sometimes last for 10 seconds, they sometimes last for 1 second. It's a total crapshoot.
-Powerups are underwhelming. Example: the speed power up (red shoe) has a nice sountrack, but you hardly notice a difference in speed.
-Sometimes Sonic just doesn't respond to moves. I've noticed this is a problem more when you're doing a wallrun than anywhere else.
That's really all I can think of. This game is definitly worth getting on sale, but I wouldn't pay the full price. The few things that I think are wrong with it really hinder the overall flow of the game, but it's not like it kills it by any means. It's still great to play, and if you were a fan of Sonic 1 & 2, then you'll enjoy this. If I could recommend a change for this game, I would recommend focusing on Sonic's speed. Increase that and you'll have a much better gaming experience. Maybe there's a mod for that...

So I tried this a while ago and said that this game must be complex, becuase I couldn't figure out anything. But I recently tried it again, and I found out that this game claims to do everything, but it just doesn't make any of the actual features fun.
There is exploration, where you take a trip, to complete a mini game. There is mining, where you take a trip to spend the next hour or so doing nothing, but wait for the ore to get mined. Then there are missions where you haul stuff back and forth for a bunch of times. Then there is pve and pvp combat, where you fly to a place, and then just wait for your ship to kill them or you get killed, there is almost nothing to do during combat, but to sit and wait.
Now all of this wouldn't make the game bad, but there is almost no content, and to fill in the lack of content, they make the grinds redicoulsly long. When ever I asked players that have played for years, they said that I had to grind for a few months before the game gets fun. That to me says that this game is just a broken game, that wants you to spend money to start having fun right away, and if you don't pay you need to grind for an unresonable amount of time. That is why I can't reccomend this, it claims to be this huge complex fun game, when it is only a normal sized idle game, that requires more input.
Oh also most of the game is behind a very expensive temporary account upgrade, that would take a few weeks or more of grinding to be able to afford it.

Once upon a time, Portal 2 was being developed as a game without portals. We all know how that worked out, but I’ve always been intrigued with that idea. The entirely new category of first person puzzler requires more than just portals after all, it needs some variety. The makers of Aperture Tag share my sentiments, and have lovingly crafted a Portal 2 mod campaign using only a paint gun and its gel mechanics. Portals are used sparingly as testing elements, but 90% of this run through Aperture’s test chambers will be spent bouncing across gaps and speeding around sharp banks, waiting for just the right moment to paint a surface or move a cube remotely. It brings a satisfying and quick new dimension to Portal levels, and even includes Workshop support for endless replayability after the main campaign is finished. Some may be put off by the idea of paying money for a mod, but anyone who takes the plunge will be pleasantly surprised by just how well this unofficial DLC stands up to the original’s sterling reputation.

Now Superfight is a game about arguments. You create a character by choosing cards from your hand aswell as one random card. Combos can look like this:
George W. Bush with Laser Eyes riding a hot air balloon
or
Helen Keller armed with a harpoon gun riding a hoverboard.
In addition you get location and event cards (that can be turned on and off when you create a lobby in-game) that further add randomness to your arguments. E.g. the above characters are fighting in heaven during a kitten stampede. And here comes the kicker: You now argue with your opponent who would win in a fight.
As an owner of the physical game, i was interested in the game once i realized an online version was in the works, but i didn't participate in the betas at all. So after purchasing it today i went in blind.
First of all, the download size is rather small. It was around 170-180mb until it was done. And that reflects when you open the game. You have several options:
Fight, where you can join or create lobbies
Spectate which shows Twitch streams for you to watch and vote on (Requires Adobe Flash and even though i have it installed it asked me to download. Still works though, if you click cancel)
Card Collection: All the decks and cards you own
Store: Just gets you to the DLC Store on Steam
And for some people there's the big elephant in the room. DLC. You can purchase extra decks for 4,99€ (or regional equivalent) that add new cards from e.g. Walking Dead or R-Rated Cards. They are optional cards, since the game already has a boatload of cards and while i bought one of the DLCs, it was a nice mix between the core-cards and the DLC cards.
Theres also an options menu which is rather slim, but it's enough for Superfight. Two sound options for Music and SFX, a Mature Content Filter, tutorial tips, fullscreen and resolution. And now come the two options that i was afraid of: Webcam and Mic. Superfight REQUIRES a microphone so you can argue with your opponent. A webcam is optional. I was afraid it would be clunky and make issues, but it worked like a charm. My mic and webcam were instantly recognized and the quality was fine.
So i searched for a game and got into my first lobby. Nobody had a webcam on so you are greeted by their steam profile pictures. The sound was really good and i played with two americans and one belgian guy. Round was alot of fun and enjoyable.
You choose your cards and once chosen your cards are on opposing sides in a standoff. You have two minutes to plead your case and then the other players choose who would win. If it happens to be a tie, a random spin decides who wins. And this is wheree twitch comes in. You can stream your game on Twitch and your viewers are able to vote on the argument winner alongside the players. It's delightful to see the loser of the argument/his cards get burned, ripped to shreds or trampled, since the animations look really nice.
I have a few little issues with Superfight though at this time:
1. No rematch button
Once the round is done, you can only choose Exit, which sends you back to the mainmenu. This is a little thing, but if you play with strangers and it works well, a rematch button would be obvious.
On a different note, a friend and i got into a round with one of the producers (who's currently at Comic-Con, HI SUMO!) and he said this would be in the works and there will be a content update next week.
2. The dangers of insecurity and webcams
This isn't a problem with the game per se, but with the community. Earlier on i watched a stream where several (by the sound of their voices) kids made fun of a large kid that dared to turn on his webcam and it made me sick. This kid embraced the game mechanic of turning on his webcam, only to get ridiculed by as*****. There needs to be a serious amount of moderation, since the internet can be a screwed up place. Methods to reporting such behaviour need to be there and taken seriously.
So after 2 hours i can say: Superfight is a well-working title that has alot of potential to become a twitch highlight game. Rounds aren't long, but offer alot of fun for a low price. Wholeheartedly recommended

Let's see what I've got to say about this game...
Feels like pieces of Counter Strike, Call of Duty and Battlefield put together into one messy Military/Army game.
Yes, I know I haven't put too many hours in A.V.A. But, in my defense, some things threw me off.
First off: (Like every single game such as this and mentioned above.) They don't really give you much training. It's more of "Just shoving weapons in your hands and forcing you out into the battlefield"
You can try to put up a fight before getting hit by a Sniper or some random soldier. (How the hell did he shoot through the wall...?)
Second: All weapons have a time limit. For what? What happens in 3 days with my M-16? Does it explode or break in half? Confiscated? Hello?

Finally: Matches and starting up.
They're pretty simple. Matchmaking with the lobbies and all that jazz. But, there were some times where I was waiting to get into a game and it just... crashes... on one occasion, even closed A.V.A. completely.
